noticias.resumen: A clear majority of European business executives believe China’s Belt and Road Initiative is more ...
noticias.texto: A clear majority of European business executives believe China’s Belt and Road Initiative is more effective than the European Union’s development strategy, according to a new 27-country survey of 536 leaders released Wednesday by London-based consultancy Polar Insight. Only 7 percent rate the EU ahead of China, while 54 percent view Beijing’s approach as superior, including relative to the EU’s Global Gateway initiative. The findings come as the EU runs a trade deficit with China of roughly €1 billion a day and as member states negotiate the next Multiannual Financial Framework, in which external action and development cooperation face potential cuts. Conducted by Polar Insight between August and October 2026 on behalf of the Strategic Communications and Advocacy Lab, the poll shows strong business support for protecting and targeting development spending as a tool of economic competitiveness and strategic competition. Four in five respondents (81 percent) say Europe’s economic resilience depends on strong ties with developing economies. Nine in ten call for targeted spending to counter strategic rivals such as China. Nearly half (48 percent) identify supply-chain security and access to critical raw materials as among the most underinvested areas of EU development policy, even though 89 percent rank it as a strategic priority. Two-thirds of executives (68 percent) consider European development cooperation relevant to their own business or sector. Overall support for the budget is high: 61 percent favour an increase in EU development aid, and 76 percent want the next seven-year spending framework to maintain or raise the development cooperation allocation. “European business sees development aid not as charity, but as a way to create long-term economic opportunities,” said James Tattersfield, CEO of Polar Insight. “Right now, executives believe Brussels is being outmanoeuvred by Beijing in the very markets that supply our critical minerals, and – as a result – want the EU to protect development spending. This comes as EU governments are considering slashes to the development budget in the next MFF.” The survey underscores broader unease over the EU-China relationship. Nine in ten respondents see countering strategic competition, including from Beijing, as an important area for investment. Business leaders frame development cooperation less as traditional aid and more as an instrument for securing supply chains, critical minerals, and long-term market access in the Global South. The results land at a sensitive moment for EU external policy. With negotiations over the next long-term budget under way, the polling provides a private-sector argument against reductions in development funding and for a more competitive European offer relative to China’s infrastructure and investment model. The survey’s release coincides with China hosting the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen on 18–19 November, where President Xi Jinping is chairing discussions among Asia-Pacific leaders – including expected participation by Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin – while European governments remain absent from the table. Caption: Dancers perform after the arrival of Prime Minister of Thailand Anutin Charnvirakul to Shenzhen Baoan International Airport for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) China 2026 Summit in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, China, 18 November 2026. EPA/ANDRES MARTINEZ CASARES / POOL

noticias.titulo: What consequences from Deutsche Bank’s massive data leak?
noticias.resumen: One of the largest leaks of confidential bank documents ever made public has hit Deutsche ...
noticias.texto: One of the largest leaks of confidential bank documents ever made public has hit Deutsche Bank, reopening debate over risk management, the effectiveness of internal controls, and the credibility of the reform path pursued by CEO Christian Sewing. More than 15 million internal files – including emails, board minutes, compliance reports, and employee communications – were provided by two whistleblowers to an international consortium of journalists. The material covers years of activity at Germany’s largest lender and sheds new light on its relationships with Russian oligarchs, financier Jeffrey Epstein, and U.S. President Donald Trump. The investigation, titled “Inside Deutsche Bank,” was published on 17 November by outlets including the Financial Times, Der Spiegel, Le Monde, and The New York Times. More than 200 journalists from around 50 organisations analysed the documents. The project was coordinated by the South African non-profit Barracuda Media, with technical support from Germany’s Data and Research Center (DARC). According to the Financial Times, the files reveal controversial conduct, control-system failures, and practices that call into question the bank’s promises of renewal. Journalists argue that, under Sewing, Deutsche Bank continued to prioritise risky commercial opportunities even when compliance officers raised concerns. Russian oligarchs, Epstein, and internal controls One of the most sensitive areas concerns Russian clients. Reports indicate the bank considered expanding business linked to oligarchs and Russian entrepreneurs shortly before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, despite warnings from internal financial-crime experts. The documents suggest commercial growth opportunities were weighed even amid reputational and geopolitical risks. The revelations do not, by themselves, prove sanctions violations, but they raise questions about the bank’s risk assessment. The Epstein chapter is particularly contentious. According to the investigation, Deutsche Bank handled roughly $582–600 million in payments flagged as suspicious and linked to Epstein – a higher figure than previously known in U.S. public debate. Epstein became a client in 2013 despite his 2008 conviction, and the relationship continued until late 2018. The files also contain new details on financial ties to Donald Trump, including the bank’s handling of his tax information during his first presidential term; Trump has described the accidental sharing of a tax document as “illegal.” These revelations add to earlier episodes that already resulted in fines and settlements for Deutsche Bank. A distinction remains between what authorities and investors already knew and genuinely new material in the leak. Confidence in Sewing-led Deutsche Bank under pressure Reputational and credibility consequences have drawn particular attention. In a 17 November editorial titled “A black day for trust in Deutsche Bank,” Handelsblatt journalist Michael Maisch criticised the bank’s initial stance that the issues largely concern the past and have already been addressed through stronger controls. Maisch summarised the bank’s response polemically as “Please move along, there’s nothing to see here.” He noted that Sewing and his team claim all questionable transactions date back “many years” and have long been resolved, with no expectation of significant financial repercussions. Markets reacted negatively: Deutsche Bank shares fell more than 5 percent and at times more than 6 percent on Tuesday. Handelsblatt argued the bank is getting off too easily. While some of Sewing’s justifications may hold, the paper stressed that the institution’s past remains so dark that every new disclosure – even of already broadly known episodes – fuels fresh investor unease. The Epstein relationship is cited as one of the most serious examples. The editorial also questions whether reforms since Sewing took charge in 2018 have genuinely changed how the bank weighs commercial opportunities against client risks. Maisch highlighted two current issues raised by the leak: the bank’s actual risk appetite (did Sewing rigorously close the chapter on scandal years, or does short-term greed still prevail?), and its ability to protect highly sensitive information. The documents reportedly include material relevant to German state security, such as accounts used under false identities by police and intelligence officers in undercover operations, according to Der Spiegel. Deutsche Bank rejected the idea that the revelations accurately describe its current state. In a 17 November statement it said many episodes date back years and that substantial changes to controls and risk management have been made under Sewing (including claims of €7 billion spent on compliance since 2019). The bank said it does not expect meaningful financial consequences from the matters that have emerged. The market reaction, however, was clearly negative. The scale of the leak itself – described by some shareholder representatives as equivalent to “detonating an atomic bomb at headquarters” – has raised separate questions about data security and internal controls, independent of the specific client relationships detailed in the files. Further reporting based on the documents is expected. The article in Italian by EUalive’s partner FocusEurope.it can be found here . Caption: The Deutsche Bank central headquarters in Frankfurt am Main, Germany, 22 July 2026. According to the investigations by several international network of journalists published on 17 November 2026, Deutsche Bank in Zurich and Geneva reportedly managed the accounts of about twenty Russian oligarchs. Two whistleblowers have leaked more than 15 million internal documents from Deutsche Bank. EPA/Matias Basualdo

noticias.titulo: Latvia’s new Kulbergs government takes office on Independence Day
noticias.resumen: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs unveiled and secured parliamentary approval for a new coalition government ...
noticias.texto: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs unveiled and secured parliamentary approval for a new coalition government on the eve of the country’s Independence Day, marking a symbolic transition as Latvia marks the restoration of its sovereignty. The Saeima approved the cabinet late on 17 November by 57 votes to 34, with the government taking office as the nation celebrates on 18 November. Kulbergs, a businessman and former automotive association leader who entered politics relatively recently, has led Latvia since May 2026. He took office after the previous coalition under Evika Siliņa collapsed amid disputes over the handling of stray drones suspected to be of Ukrainian origin that entered Latvian airspace. His United List alliance, a centre-right grouping of regionalist and green-conservative forces, won 35.3 percent of the vote and roughly 41 seats in the 3 October parliamentary election – the strongest result for any political force since Latvia regained independence in 1991. The alliance formed a two-party coalition with the national-conservative National Alliance, together holding a narrow majority of 51 seats in the 100-member Saeima. Some additional support from deputies of the opposition Latvia First party helped secure the 57-vote margin. An all-ECR coalition The new government is an all-ECR coalition, as both the United List and National Alliance sit in the European Conservatives and Reformists Group in the European Parliament. The ECR Group welcomed the outcome, with Co-Chairman Nicola Procaccini congratulating Kulbergs and the parties for forming a government “united by a commitment to security, economic responsibility and Latvia’s firm place in the West.” Co-Chairman Patryk Jaki described it as “excellent news for Latvia and for our political family,” stressing the mandate for change on security, bureaucracy reduction, and economic opportunity. Latvian ECR MEPs, including Reinis Pozņaks (United List), Roberts Zīle (National Alliance), and Rihards Kols (National Alliance), echoed the focus on cutting bureaucracy, attracting investment, strengthening resilience, energy security, national interests, and NATO’s eastern flank. A distinctive feature of the cabinet is the appointment of several nominally non-partisan technocrats to key posts. Four of the 13 ministries are headed by non-aligned candidates, while the remainder go to members of the United List and National Alliance. Notable nominees include Kārlis Purgailis, chief economist at Citadele Bank and an external economic adviser to Kulbergs, as finance minister; Ģirts Jaunzems, a career diplomat and former ambassador to Uzbekistan, as foreign minister; and Normunds Staņēvičs, a businessman and board member of Amber Beverage Group who previously headed a major Riga hospital, as health minister. Commentators have welcomed the inclusion of specialists for their apparent expertise and impartiality, but others have noted personal connections – including former classmates and private-sector colleagues of the prime minister. Defence Minister Raivis Melnis and Interior Minister Jānis Dombrava are among those retaining posts, while the cabinet remains male-dominated, with only one woman (Welfare Minister Ilze Indriksone) among its members. Kulbergs has outlined priorities centred on economic growth after more than a decade of underperformance relative to other Baltic states, attracting investment, reducing bureaucracy and the size of the public sector, and accelerating decision-making. The coalition agreement commits to continued military, political, and economic support for Ukraine until victory, promotion of Ukraine’s EU and NATO path, and the severing of economic ties with Russia and Belarus. Security remains central, building on Kulbergs’ earlier emphasis on air defence and border measures following the drone incidents that brought him to power. He has described the government’s approach as characterised by “speed, plain language and responsibility,” with cutting inefficiency, bureaucracy and excess public spending as a key theme. The narrow majority and the compressed timeline – the lineup was presented on the morning of the vote and approved after more than seven hours of debate that same evening – drew criticism in the chamber over haste and limited opportunity for public scrutiny ahead of the Independence Day deadline. Latvia has a long record of governments failing to complete full terms, and the loose structure of the United List adds another layer of uncertainty. Pro-Russian parties increased their representation but remain outside government influence. Caption: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs (C) attends the 15th Parliament (Saeima) an extraordinary plenary session, to hold a vote of confidence on the new government in Riga, Latvia, 17 November 2026. The proposed government is formed by the United List (Apvienotais saraksts) and the National Alliance (Nacionala apvieniba), which together hold a majority of 51 out of 100 seats in Parliament. EPA/TOMS KALNINS

noticias.titulo: Germany and Britain reject U.S. criticism of Ukraine’s deep strikes as “stupid”
noticias.resumen: Germany and Britain sharply rebuffed criticism from a senior U.S. Pentagon official of Ukraine’s long-range ...
noticias.texto: Germany and Britain sharply rebuffed criticism from a senior U.S. Pentagon official of Ukraine’s long-range strikes inside Russia, exposing a clear divide among Kyiv’s backers over strategy at a meeting of the Ukraine Defence Contact Group at NATO headquarters on 17 November. U.S. Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby argued that Ukraine’s deep-strike campaign has not been effective in ending the war or slowing Russian advances on the front line. In remarks delivered at the gathering, he said the public focus on such strikes as a way to inflict pain on the Russian population overlooks their limited impact. He specifically warned that attacks on commercial targets, including warehouses of the Russian online retailer Wildberries, have likely hardened Russian public resolve and increased the Kremlin’s willingness to escalate. Colby added that the balance of advantage in deep strikes may favor Moscow and urged allies to prioritize support for Ukraine’s ability to hold the front line and make gains, including through mid-range strikes that interdict logistics. He noted recent Ukrainian success in this approach, citing territorial gains and high Russian casualties in October. German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius rejected the criticism outright. Asked about Colby’s position, he described criticizing strikes on strategic military and military-used targets inside Russia as “quite a stupid thing.” Pistorius argued that attention should instead focus on what he called Russia’s “terroristic strikes every night and every day” on Ukraine’s energy, water, and heating infrastructure. He characterized those Russian attacks as a form of terrorism and defended Ukrainian strikes against non-civilian targets as legal and legitimate. Germany has previously lifted range restrictions on weapons it supplies to Ukraine. British Defence Secretary Wes Streeting, who co-chaired the meeting with Pistorius, took a similar stance. He said it is not for outside partners to dictate how Ukraine fights its war and that Ukraine’s deep-strike capability has helped degrade President Vladimir Putin’s war machine, buying time and saving lives. Streeting also referenced Ukrainian ingenuity in response to Russian aggression. Ukrainian Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara, also in Brussels, said Kyiv’s strikes respond to Russian attacks and pointed to a recent Ukrainian operation against the Crimean Bridge. He indicated plans to expand Ukraine’s deep-strike capabilities significantly next year. The exchange occurred as the United States, under the Trump administration, has signaled a preference for Europe to assume greater responsibility for supporting Ukraine while prioritizing U.S. readiness elsewhere. It also comes ahead of expected U.S.-led peace talks involving Ukraine and Russia. Colby’s remarks emphasized that a successful Ukrainian “denial defense” on the front line reduces the incentives for Moscow to continue the war, while stressing continued U.S. commitment to a durable peace and the need for sustained European funding and industrial capacity for munitions. Caption: US Under Secretary of Defense for Policy Elbridge Colby, German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius, and British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting attend a meeting of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group at the Alliance’s headquarters in Brussels, Belgium, 17 November 2026. The meeting, co-chaired by the United Kingdom and Germany, focuses on coordinating military support for Ukraine, including strengthening air defenses and protecting energy infrastructure against Russian attacks ahead of winter. EPA/OLIVIER HOSLET

noticias.titulo: Tech outage wave reaches U.S. government; Trump says all is ‘fine’
noticias.resumen: Technology outages that shut down email for many companies and grounded thousands of flights over ...
noticias.texto: Technology outages that shut down email for many companies and grounded thousands of flights over the past few days extended ​to the U.S. National Security Agency on Tuesday, as President Donald Trump’s administration downplayed concerns about a broader problem. The NSA said its network experienced a “temporary degradation” during routine ‌maintenance, but that “mission-critical capabilities” remained operational. The series of disruptions to critical systems, which also touched the banking system on Monday, prompted even some Trump allies to demand more information. “If this is all a coincidence, it’s like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world,” U.S. Senator Josh Hawley, a Missouri Republican, told reporters. Trump earlier played down the incidents, which raised questions of whether the government and private sector had moved too quickly in cutting tech staff. “It’s like ​when you’re big and powerful, and you have all the money. Things like that happen. It’s fine,” Trump told reporters in Manila, where he was attending meetings with the Association ​of Southeast Asian Nations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who doubles as national security adviser, acknowledged the incidents were “unsettling” but said they were completely unrelated and ⁠that there was “zero evidence” they were caused by “nefarious actors.” “We are not under systemic attack,” he told reporters in Manila. Daily downtime Technology-related disruptions have hit every weekday since Thursday, when a Microsoft outage disrupted many of ​its services, including email. Faxes, phones and Bluetooth: Microsoft outage forces businesses to find fixes The next day, the Federal Aviation Administration called for a nationwide ground stop that lasted 4-1/2 hours, the longest halt to U.S. air travel since the attacks of September 11, 2001. U.S. to resume flights after air traffic network failure sparks chaos The spate ​of outages included a United Airlines technology failure on Monday that delayed about 150 flights on the same day that a JPMorgan Chase software problem disrupted some banking services. On Tuesday, Apple said it was working to restore its systems after an internal update caused an outage that affected customer services including iCloud and Apple Pay. The issue was not caused by a cyberattack, Apple said. Insurance provider Marsh also said on Tuesday its clients reported 105 cyber incidents in the last two ​weeks of October – more than double the 48 recorded in the final two weeks of May. Experts worry that AI tools are feeding a surge of cyberactivity, with cybersecurity companies regularly turning up examples of ​hackers using AI to launch scores of intrusions at once. “The recent string of major disruptions across industries highlights how deeply interconnected our digital infrastructure has become, and how a single technical failure or software update can cascade with ‌outsized effects ⁠across critical systems,” said Cynthia Kaiser, a former senior FBI cyber official and current senior vice president of cybersecurity firm Halcyon’s Ransomware Research Center. Jay Clayton, the US director of national intelligence, attributed the NSA outage to patches deployed for a PHP vulnerability discovered using AI last month – a bug that could let hackers remotely take control of servers. “Everybody recognizes it’s time to upgrade their systems, and as they upgrade them, they’re not coming back as expected in all cases, and in some cases, systems have to hand off to other systems, and those handoffs are not coming back as expected,” Clayton told the “Claman ​Countdown” program on Fox Business. The NSA and Wall Street ​executives have told members of Congress the ⁠vulnerabilities that needed fixing were identified by artificial intelligence, the Washington Sun reported, citing three sources familiar with the private conversations. The fixes temporarily overwhelmed the systems, the Sun reported. Outages follow layoffs, warnings At many organizations – both private and government – the outages follow layoffs and, in some cases, ​explicit warnings about potential disruptions. At the FAA, which was hit by Elon Musk-driven job cuts after Trump took office last year, Congress warned the ​agency’s sped-up modernisation effort ⁠was poorly organised and could trigger service outages. United Airlines said last year that AI advances had helped it cut management headcount by 4% and that it planned to cut by an additional 4% this year. At Microsoft, the email outage came a month after the company said it was offering buyouts to a quarter of its global workforce, a move that follows previous headcount reductions. While there is no evidence job losses at ⁠any of these ​places led to the disruptions, one tech labour organszer said cuts tended to make safety margins thinner. “Part of the resilience ​of a system comes from people who are experienced with a system,” said Liz Fong-Jones, who has worked for 20 years on software resilience issues. With Reuters Caption: Visual by the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security [@cybercentre_ca on X]

noticias.titulo: China’s Xi calls for free and open trade at APEC summit
noticias.resumen: Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday urged support for “free and open trade,” while expressing ...
noticias.texto: Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday urged support for “free and open trade,” while expressing opposition to “protectionism” in an opening speech at an Asia-Pacific ‌summit where he was due to meet his U.S. and Russian counterparts. Xi’s remarks came after Washington announced further restrictions on China’s access to advanced AI chips from companies such as Nvidia, which could further complicate a fragile trade truce with Beijing. China has pledged to retaliate. “We must firmly uphold the rules-based multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organization at its core, support free and ​open trade and investment, maintain the stability and smooth operation of global industrial and supply chains,” Xi told an audience of business executives, after posing ​a series of rhetorical questions on how the Asia Pacific should respond to a changing world. Western trade partners have criticised China ⁠for running annual trade surpluses in excess of $1 trillion through policies that support its manufacturing sector at the expense of its consumers. Beijing says its growth model is ​appropriate for an economy still catching up with the world’s richest, but Washington, Brussels and others are concerned about China’s supply chain dominance providing the country with geopolitical ​leverage and say its policies threaten their industries and jobs. Xi said China will continue to invest in its industrial complex and develop new technologies that would also benefit other countries. The world’s second-largest economy will lower tariffs and further open up its markets, while standing up against protectionism and unilateralism, he added. His “message is likely to resonate with many Global South countries and reinforces Beijing’s ​effort to contrast its technology strategy with that of Washington,” said George Chen, partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group. High-stakes meetings Xi was at the ​opening of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation CEOs summit in the southern Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen, ahead of a gathering of the member states’ leaders in the evening. Russian President Vladimir Putin landed overnight, ‌after Ukraine ⁠destroyed the vital Kerch road bridge linking Crimea to Russia in a major blow to his four-year-old war. Second attack on the Crimean Bridge in two days: what is known U.S. President Donald Trump was due to arrive later on Wednesday after concluding meetings with Southeast Asian and other regional leaders in Manila. The three leaders are set for high-stakes talks on Thursday on the Iran and Ukraine wars, with flashpoints such as trade, AI and nuclear weapons also on the agenda. The U.S. president also floated the possibility that he might meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, but that ​has not been confirmed. Trump’s trip to Asia ​is his first since his Republican ⁠Party’s defeat in midterm elections, while allegations involving Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy add to the tension. Still, most analysts expect Washington and Beijing to keep ties relatively stable as Trump and Xi are due to meet for the fourth ​time this year at the Group of 20 gathering in Miami in December. Trump and Xi have a working lunch on ​Thursday before the two ⁠meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The three-way meeting has drawn comparisons with the 1945 Yalta Conference between the U.S., Britain and the Soviet Union that formalized spheres of influence, set the stage for the post-World War Two order and became shorthand for great-power deals imposed on smaller countries. No new Yalta: Russia’s demands ignore the facts on the ground The Kremlin this week dismissed the comparisons as “games of political scientists,” but said ⁠the meeting ​will have a major impact on global affairs. Beijing said the trilateral is of “groundbreaking significance” and ​will promote world peace. But smaller powers in Europe and Asia not at the table fear any deal that might emerge between the three men that disregards their security interests. On Tuesday, Taiwan and Japan flagged incursions ​by Russian aircraft into their airspace. With Reuters Caption: Chinese President Xi Jinping (top C) speaks at the 2026 APEC CEO Summit held ahead of the APEC China 2026 summit in Shenzhen, China, 18 November 2026. EPA/NG HAN GUAN / POOL

noticias.titulo: Janša ally to lead Slovenian parliamentary inquiry into “Black Cube” affair
noticias.resumen: Slovenia’s parliament is preparing to launch an inquiry into the alleged political misuse of the ...
noticias.texto: Slovenia’s parliament is preparing to launch an inquiry into the alleged political misuse of the country’s intelligence agency SOVA and police in connection with the Black Cube affair, which erupted shortly before the parliamentary elections in March 2026. The private Israeli intelligence firm Black Cube helped Janša win the elections and bring down the government of Robert Golob, critical of Israel’s Gaza war. In contrast, Janša’s cabinet turned to be Israel’s best ally in the EU. All 12 members present voted in favour of the proposal, Slovenian broadcaster N1 reported. The commission is expected to be chaired by Anja Bah Žibert, an MP from Janša’s ruling Slovenian Democratic Party (SDS). Nedeljko Todorović, from the populist Resni.ca party, which supports the government in parliament, is proposed as deputy chair. The appointment of an MP from the ruling party to lead the investigation raises eyebrows, as the affair has also raised questions about the prime minister’s possible contacts with the Israeli private intelligence firm. The parliamentary Committee on Mandates and Elections on Monday unanimously approved the proposed membership of an investigative commission tasked with examining suspicions of political interference in the work of the intelligence and law enforcement services. The proposed commission will investigate alleged political instrumentalisation and abuse of intelligence and investigative capabilities, as well as attempts to influence elections. One of its central tasks will be to examine the handling and public disclosure of information concerning the Black Cube affair. The investigation was requested by SDS, Resni.ca and the political grouping comprising New Slovenia (NSi), the Slovenian People’s Party (SLS) and Focus. Its proposed membership also includes representatives of the Freedom Movement (Svoboda), the Social Democrats (SD), Levica and the Democrats, giving both government and opposition parties a place on the panel. However, the decision to put an SDS MP in the chair is likely to attract scrutiny, given that the investigation could touch on allegations concerning Janša himself. Covert recordings and alleged foreign interference The Black Cube affair became one of the defining controversies of Slovenia’s parliamentary election campaign in March 2026, after a series of secretly recorded conversations involving prominent Slovenian figures appeared online. The recordings were published on a website called Anti Corruption 2026, which presented them as evidence of alleged corruption within the political establishment surrounding then-prime minister Robert Golob. The website did not identify its owners, editors or contact details. Those targeted had reportedly been invited to what they believed were legitimate business meetings organised by a purported British investment fund, Stockard Capital. The meetings were subsequently revealed to have been arranged under false pretences, with participants secretly recorded. Among those featured in the videos were former justice minister Dominika Švarc Pipan, lawyer Nina Zidar Klemenčič, lobbyist Rok Hodej and businessman Dejan Paravan. An investigation published by Slovenian weekly Mladina on 16 March, prepared by investigative journalists, linked the operation to Black Cube private intelligence company. Kompromat and “black PR” against the government of Slovenia The investigation drew parallels with methods previously attributed to the Israeli company in other countries, particularly Hungary, where operatives posing as business contacts had secretly recorded journalists and civil society activists ahead of elections. The Slovenian investigators also examined flight records and other publicly available information concerning visits by Black Cube representatives to the country. They alleged that the company’s representatives had met SDS leader Janez Janša in Ljubljana on 22 December 2025, although this claim was not independently confirmed by the intelligence agency. Janša denied meeting the company. According to N1, SOVA already confirmed that representatives of Black Cube had been in Slovenia on 22 December 2025, but did not have information confirming that they had met Janša. On 18 March State Secretary for National and International Security Vojko Volk said the company’s methods included recruiting individuals through fake online profiles, using operatives with false identities to gather information and arranging meetings in hotels, restaurants and other public places. According to the previous government, such operations typically involved publishing manipulated material at a carefully selected moment, in this case shortly before an election, with the aim of politically discrediting targets. On 20 March SOVA director Joško Kadivnik presented what the government described as material evidence linking three Black Cube representatives to a visit to Trstenjakova Street 8 in Ljubljana, where SDS has its headquarters. A company with a controversial international record Black Cube is an Israeli private intelligence company founded by former members of the country’s intelligence and military establishments. It has operated internationally on behalf of private clients, often in connection with commercial disputes, litigation and investigations. However, the company has repeatedly attracted controversy over undercover operations involving journalists, activists and public figures. One of its most notorious cases involved its work for Hollywood producer Harvey Weinstein. In 2017, the company apologised after operatives working under false identities were reported to have monitored journalists and individuals involved in investigating allegations of sexual misconduct against Weinstein. The company has also been linked to operations in Hungary ahead of the 2018 and 2022 parliamentary elections. The Slovenian affair also attracted international attention because of the potential implications for electoral integrity and foreign interference in EU member states. Then-prime minister Robert Golob raised the issue with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen in March, describing the alleged operation as a serious case of foreign information manipulation and interference. Janša’s reversal: Slovenia’s new government signals strong pivot toward Israel Sources: N1 Slovenia, Dnevnik Slovenia, BGNES Caption: Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Jansa arrives for a European Council summit in Brussels, Belgium, 15 October 2026. European Union (EU) heads of state and government are meeting for a two-day summit on 15 and 16 October 2026 focusing on European competitiveness and energy prices, the EU’s long-term budget for 2028-2034, continued support for Ukraine, European security and defence, migration, enlargement and reforms, and developments in the Middle East. EPA/OLIVIER MATTHYS

noticias.titulo: LPG tanker sinks off Bulgaria after reported drone attack, all 19 crew rescued
noticias.resumen: A liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) tanker sank in Bulgaria’s Black Sea exclusive economic zone on ...
noticias.texto: A liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) tanker sank in Bulgaria’s Black Sea exclusive economic zone on Tuesday after reportedly being hit by drones, in the latest incident involving commercial shipping in the western Black Sea. All 19 members of the crew, all Filipino nationals, were rescued unharmed, with two sustaining minor injuries. The Liberian-flagged GAS HUSKY was reported to have been struck about 55 nautical miles south-east of Varna. The Romanian Naval Authority was the first to report that the vessel had been attacked by drones. The ship’s captain subsequently confirmed that it had been hit, although Bulgarian authorities have not officially established the cause of the sinking. According to the captain, the tanker was struck by four drones shortly after midnight, in the area of the engine room and the bridge. Maritime.bg also reported, citing a source at the company managing the vessel, that it had been attacked by maritime drone as well. The ship disappeared from radar shortly after midnight while sailing from Alexandria, Egypt, to the Romanian port of Midia. Its emergency position-indicating radio beacon (EPIRB) was activated at 08:02 local time on Tuesday, sending a distress signal from a position approximately 50 nautical miles east of the Bulgarian coastal town of Byala. The vessel was carrying 3,403.032 metric tonnes of liquefied gas, according to information reported by Bulgarian media. Romanian news agency AGERPRES reported that it was transporting propane. The tanker was operated by the Greece-based Stealth Maritime Corporation, according to Romanian media reports. Military aircraft deployed in rescue operation Bulgaria launched an air and sea search-and-rescue operation after the emergency signal was detected. An Su-25 aircraft took off from the air base in Balchik at 10:25 local time to survey the area, while a Cougar helicopter was activated to rescue the crew. A second Su-25 was also sent towards the site shortly after 11:00. A rescue raft carrying survivors was spotted in the water. The crew members were evacuated by helicopter and transported to the Chaika naval air base near Varna. The operation was coordinated by Bulgaria’s Maritime Administration, with the Air Force, Border Police and emergency medical services taking part. It was called off at 13:15, after all crew members had been brought to safety. The sinking occurred in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone (EEZ), outside its 12-nautical-mile territorial sea. Although the area is not part of Bulgaria’s territorial waters, the country has specific rights and responsibilities there, including in relation to maritime resources and certain activities. Second ship lost in two days The incident came less than 24 hours after the cargo vessel BETUL 8 was hit by maritime drones and capsized in the same area. The Somali-flagged ship was carrying more than 3,000 tonnes of wheat from the Romanian port of Tulcea to Egypt. Its 12-member crew, comprising eight Turkish and four Azerbaijani nationals, was rescued by Bulgarian military helicopters after abandoning the vessel. The last known position of GAS HUSKY was approximately 14.5 nautical miles from the location where BETUL 8 capsized. If the reported drone attack on the tanker is confirmed, it would be the seventh vessel struck in Bulgaria’s Black Sea waters over the past six weeks. The incidents are part of a wider series of attacks and maritime emergencies affecting commercial shipping in the western Black Sea. Several vessels have been hit by drones in the Bulgarian and Romanian exclusive economic zones in recent weeks, with some sinking and sailors losing their lives. Bulgarian authorities have repeatedly said they lack conclusive evidence identifying the source of the attacks. They have nevertheless acknowledged that the available indications point towards Russia. The government has so far refrained from publicly attributing responsibility for the individual incidents. “We will certainly not hide the truth about the attacks, but making accusations against anyone could draw us into a war,” Deputy Prime Minister Ivo Hristov told the Bulgarian National Television a couple of days ago. Opposition calls for national security meeting The opposition coalition Democratic Bulgaria has called on President Iliana Iotova to convene the Consultative Council for National Security, citing both the repeated attacks on commercial vessels in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone and Russian demands made in Abu Dhabi concerning restrictions on allied defence in Europe. The party wants the council to hear from the security services, the military and the ministers responsible, and to recommend concrete measures to improve maritime security. These should include permanent coordination with Romania and Turkey, anti-drone capabilities and better protection for shipping and critical infrastructure. Democratic Bulgaria also called for clear deadlines, designated institutions and funding for the proposed measures. On the wider security issue, the party said the council should make clear that Bulgaria rejects any new spheres of influence or agreements allowing the Kremlin to restrict allied presence and defence in the country. “Bulgaria’s security cannot be traded for reservations, insinuations and keeping a low profile,” the party said. Last month, Bulgaria proposed negotiations among the six Black Sea littoral states including the agressor Russia – to seek a moratorium on hostilities and turn the sea into a “zone of shared security”. The proposal was adopted at meeting of the Consultative Council for National Security and announced by Iotova, who, like Prime Minister Rumen Radev, has taken positions widely seen as favourable to Moscow. Radev’s political party, Progressive Bulgaria, holds an outright majority in parliament, giving his government a free hand. Both leaders have advocated dialogue with Russia and opposed military support for Ukraine. Iotova said Sofia should take an active role in building consensus and bring the issue to European forums, particularly the EU summit. Sources: Segabg.com, BGNES, Maritime bg Caption: Footage from the rescue operation involving the GAS HUSKY, released by Bulgaria’s Defence Ministry on Tuesday.

noticias.titulo: Diputación Permanente del Congreso
noticias.texto:
En directo: La Diputación Permanente del Congreso vota los siete últimos decretos-leyes del Gobierno
- Se debaten medidas para las víctimas del accidente de Urda, de apoyo a Ceuta y al transporte ferroviario
- También tres decretos para ampliar la protección de la Seguridad Social a "colectivos vulnerables"
La Diputación Permanente del Congreso —único órgano parlamentario que sigue activo tras la disolución de las Cortes— debate y vota este miércoles los siete últimos reales decretos-leyes aprobados este mes por el Consejo de Ministros con medidas para asuntos de urgencia como las ayudas para las víctimas del accidente de trenes de Urda, de apoyo financiero a Ceuta y dirigidas a paliar los efectos de la dana Adam.
Estos decretos leyes entran en vigor al publicarse en el Boletín Oficial del Estado (BOE), pero deben votarse en el Congreso en el plazo de 30 días para decidir si se convalidan o se derogan. Como la Cámara se disolvió al convocarse las elecciones, esa validación se asigna a la Diputación Permanente, el órgano parlamentario que sustituye al Pleno.
El Gobierno y sus socios pueden sacar adelante los decretos sin necesidad de Junts en la diputación permanente, ya que en este órgano que cuenta con 69 miembros, PSOE, Sumar, ERC, Bildu y Podemos, que representa al Grupo Mixto, suman 34 votos; frente a los 34 de PP, Vox y Junts, por lo que el voto del PNV resulta decisivo para alcanzar una mayoría de 35.
Torres defiende los reales decretos de apoyo a Ceuta y para paliar los efectos de la dana Adam
El ministro de Política Territorial y Memoria Democrática, Ángel Víctor Torres, ha sido el encargado de defender los reales decretos con medidas económicas de apoyo para Ceuta tras la entrada masiva de inmigrantes de finales de julio, que contempla subvenciones directas por 45,32 millones de euros, y las ayudas para paliar los efectos de la dana Adam en la Comunidad Valenciana con medidas "urgentes" por importe de 182,2 millones de euros, fiscales y financieras, dirigidas entre otros, a la agricultura y el turismo.
En Ceuta, Torres ha cifrado en 5.037 personas migrantes las que están siendo atendidas por los recursos del Estado de los que 532 son menores no acompañados que están en los dispositivos de mayores de edad, aunque, según ha señalado, esa competencia es de la ciudad. Del total de personas que siguen en la ciudad autónoma, 4.505 son responsabilidad del Gobierno central.
En cuanto a los menores no acompañados, a los 532 que están siendo atendidos en recursos del Ejecutivo central, ha dicho que se suman 3.156 que están recibiendo la asistencia del Gobierno local, para lo que se ha puesto en manos de la ciudad autónoma 88 millones de euros. El ministro ha anunciado que todos los asentamientos están desalojados y ya no hay grupos pernoctando en Ceuta y que se ha decidido bajar a nivel 1 el nivel de protección marítima del puerto, al no haber ya presencia de migrantes.
"Se recupera la normalidad", ha señalado el ministro, que también ha avanzado que este miércoles comienzan las obras de ampliación del espigón y del obstáculo flotante que pasará a tener más de medio kilómetro que se prolongarán alrededor de tres meses.
El PP acusa al Gobierno de "negligencia" en Ceuta y "abandono" de las infraestructuras
La diputada del PP, Sofía Acedo Reyes, ha advertido al Ejecutivo que la ciudad autónoma de Ceuta "no va a recuperar la normalidad con 45 millones de euros", sólo "empezará a recuperar la normalidad el día que salgan todos los que invadieron la ciudad el 30 y 31 de julio", y lo ha acusado de "abandonar" a los ceutíes que llevan 100 días "invadidos" poniendo como ejemplo a las mujeres que "siguen sin poder caminar tranquilamente" después de más de una treintena de agresiones sexuales.
"¿Son ustedes conscientes de las consecuencias que ha provocado la negligencia de su Gobierno?", ha dicho la diputada que considera que no tienen "legitimidad moral y política para solucionar" lo que ellos mismos han provocado y ha criticado que el real decreto hable de "crisis migratoria" cuando fue "una invasión, una violación de la integridad territorial como dijo Sánchez". También ha dicho que hablan de "respuesta humanitaria", pero hay "140 personas muertas de las que no se acuerdan por su negligencia, esto sí que es inhumano".
En relación con el segundo decreto ley a debate, con ayudas para paliar los efectos de la dana Adam, la diputada del PP, Belén Hoyo Juliá, ha advertido que "el miedo" de los valencianos sigue y se ha preguntado si están más protegidos. "Hay que hacer infraestructuras para proteger a la gente, Sánchez no ha hecho ninguna", ha advertido la diputada que ha recordado los accidentes ferroviarios en Adamuz y Urda y ha acusado al Gobierno de "abandono de las infraestructuras".
"Lo importante no es cuanto se anuncia sino cuánto se ejecuta", ha señalado la diputada, que acusa al Ejecutivo central de que "presume haber movilizado 16.000 millones para la reconstrucción de Valencia" pero más de 7.000 millones "son del consorcio de compensación de seguros" y las ha pedido que "no intenten engañar".
Sumar y Podemos denuncian torturas a los migrantes en Ceuta y señalan a Marruecos: "No son piezas de ajedrez"
Por parte de Sumar —socio del PSOE en el Gobierno de coalición— la portavoz Aina Vidal, ha denunciado los casos de torturas, hasta 50 documentados por la organización Amnistía Internacional , según ha asegurado, presuntas agresiones cometidos por españoles, miembros de las Fuerzas Armadas contra personas migrantes.
Vidal ha calificado de "muy grave" lo ocurrido el 30 y 31 de julio en la ciudad autónoma y ha llamado a "reconocer la humanidad" de los vecinos que "han abierto su casa, compartido su comida y quienes han utilizado sufrimiento para alimentar miedo, odio, racismo". Vidal ha pedido hablar de "Marruecos, Trump y Netanyahu, ¿quién se beneficia de convertir a miles de personas en instrumentos, material fungible?" y que se investigue para "exigir responsabilidades" porque "las personas migrantes no son piezas de ajedrez, son personas".
La diputada y líder de Podemos, Ione Belarra, primera en tomar la palabra después de Torres ha denunciado los casos de torturas, más de 22 que la organización Amnistía Internacional ha documentado y ha citado varios de los testimonios que hablan de persecuciones, agresiones nocturnas, patadas, puñetazos y robo de pertenencias. Unos testimonios que según ha explicado, señalan especialmente a los regulares y la legión.
"¿Está de acuerdo con esto?", ha dicho Belarra al ministro Torres, "¿el Gobierno está de acuerdo con que los recibamos a palos?", y le ha preguntado por qué "no han abierto una investigación independiente y "expulsado a las fuerzas y cuerpos que acometen estas torturas".
Vox ve la "invasión" de Ceuta motivo de "una declaración de guerra", pide la "defensa permanente" del Ejército y una "acción penal" contra el Gobierno
El diputado de Vox, Sánchez García, ha tomado la palabra y ha comenzado respondiendo a las portavoces de Sumar y Podemos cuya voz ha calificado de "altisonante, hueca y ajena a las preocupaciones de los españoles" sobre la situación de Ceuta. El diputado ha acusado a estas formaciones de ser "los primeros que expanden esas especies mentirosas y de imputar delitos de odio" y ha pedido a Belarra que mire las acepciones de la palabra "invasión" en el diccionario de la Real Academia Española.
Ceuta, según el diputado de Vox, precisa de una "defensa militar permanente" porque "desde el siglo XIX", al igual que Melilla, "son reivindicadas por el sultanato de Marruecos con episodios bélicos" y este es el último dicen que no es invasión esto es casus belli", motivo, ha dicho para "declarar una guerra".
Por ello, ha acusado al Gobierno de "pasar de puntillas" y de una "pasividad" que "constituye una actuación, comportamiento penalmente relevante que se llama traición del presidente y ministros" y ha pedido el ejercicio de la "acción penal" promovida por la Cámara.
Saiz defiende los decretos sociales para ampliar la protección de la Seguridad Social en casos de violencia de género, familias monoparentales y dependencia
La ministra de Inclusión, Seguridad Social y Migraciones, Elma Saiz, ha pedido a los grupos parlamentarios su apoyo al real decreto 31/2026 para la mejora de la "acción protectora" de la Seguridad Social "convencida" de que la Cámara "comparte el principio básico" de que la "protección publica debe evolucionar al ritmo que lo hace la evolución social".
Con estos reales decretos, ha dicho la ministra, se corrigen "situaciones de desprotección" y "se fortalece" la cobertura de colectivos "vulnerables", con medidas como la ampliación de los supuestos de incapacidad temporal por patologías incapacitantes asociadas a la menopausia y las lesiones derivadas de la violencia de género, las prestaciones por cuidado de menores con enfermedades graves, los requisitos de acceso a la pensión de viudedad para parejas de hecho con hijos en común y las pensiones de orfandad en casos de violencia contra la mujer.
También se debate un decreto con medidas para el reconocimiento y protección de las familias monoparentales, con una categoría especial para determinados supuestos, como las familias con dos o más hijos, con un hijo y rentas bajas o con un hijo con discapacidad. También se amplía la cobertura de los anticipos del Fondo de Garantía del Pago de Alimentos y se debate un decreto ley para el despliegue de la reforma del Sistema para la Autonomía y Atención a la Dependencia, que fija las cuantías mensuales mínimas de protección en 90 euros para la dependencia moderada, 260 euros para la severa y 660 euros para la gran dependencia, además de regular suplementos de crédito para financiar el nivel acordado de protección en 2027.
Los dos siguientes decretos a debate serán los aprobados por el Consejo de Ministros tras la tragedia ferroviaria de Urda (Toledo), uno de ayudas a las víctimas y otro de medidas urgentes para reforzar la seguridad operacional en el transporte ferroviario y la protección social del personal ferroviario.
El primero establece ayudas por fallecimiento y lesiones que oscilan entre los 2.404 y los 84.141 euros, además de medidas de protección de los consumidores, como la limitación de los precios abusivos que se produce situaciones de emergencia por parte de algunos operadores de transportes.
El segundo modifica la regulación sobre los tiempos de conducción de trenes, los coeficientes reductores de la edad de jubilación de determinadas categorías ferroviarias y la supervisión de la Agencia Estatal de Seguridad Ferroviaria, tal y como explicó el ya exministro de Transportes Oscar Puente en la Diputación Permanente de la semana pasada.

noticias.titulo: Feijóo niega que Vox le haya planteado "ninguna línea incruzable" y advierte: no pactará "a cualquier precio"
noticias.texto:
Feijóo dice que Vox no le ha planteado "ninguna línea incruzable" y advierte de que no pactará "a cualquier precio"
- Vuelve a defender sus pactos con Vox en una entrevista en el podcast 'El sentido de la birra'
- Consulta el comparador de programas electorales para los comicios del 29-N
El candidato del PP a la Presidencia del Gobierno el 29-N, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, ha asegurado que por el "momento" Vox no le ha planteado "ninguna línea incruzable" en los Ejecutivos autonómicos en los que gobiernan en coalición, y aunque no ha descartado ningún nuevo pacto con los de Santiago Abascal si los necesitara tras las elecciones generales, ha avisado de que no quiere "ser será presidente pactando a cualquier precio".
"A mí no me ha planteado Vox en este momento ninguna línea incruzable. En las cuatro comunidades autónómas en las que gobernamos juntos, Vox no ha planteado nada que digamos que no es posible. Y cuando lo ha planteado, hemos dicho que no es legal y si no es legal, nosotros no vamos a hacer cosas fuera de la ley", ha respondido tajante en una entrevista en el podcast 'El sentido de la birra' que se ha publicado este miércoles.
A un día del debate cara a cara entre los dos candidatos de los partidos con más posibilidades de llegar a la Moncloa, el también líder del PP ha liberado su agenda de actos públicos, y ha limitado su presencia en este dia de campaña electoral a varias entrevistas en diferentes formatos para llegar a nuevos posibles votantes.
No es la primera vez en esta campaña que Feijóo defiende sus pactos con Vox. Este martes aseguró también que se sentía "más cerca" de Santiago Abascal que del líder de EH Bildu, Arnaldo Otegi, como modo de reproche al candidato socialista, Pedro Sánchez, que pactó su investidura en 2023 con los 'abertzales'.
Este miércoles ha confirmado que mantiene conversaciones "fluidas" con Abascal, sobre todo en el último año, y ha asegurado que no tiene "ninguna duda del origen democrático" del líder de Vox. Por contra, ha insistido en que no pactará con quien le "exija excarcelar etarras", en referencia precisamente a EH Bildu.
No obstante, Feijóo ha recordado que el PP estableció "un marco de negociación" antes de pactar con Vox los Gobiernos autonómicos de Extremadura, Aragón, Castilla y León y Andalucía, y ha ratificado que lo va a "respetar" en próximas negociaciones con los de Santiago Abascal.
Asegura que no habrá retrocesos en el aborto y derechos LGTBI
Preguntado por qué le diría a la gente que tiene miedo de que el PP pacte con Vox por asuntos como el derecho al aborto, la eutanasia o las leyes sobre el colectivo LGTBI, Feijóo ha garantizado que "no va a haber ningún retroceso" en derechos si llega a la Moncloa, y ha opinado que el retroceso sería "quedarse con 131 diputados, con tu hermano condenado, tu mujer pendiente de juicio y tus dos manos derechas, uno en la cárcel, otro pendiente de juicio", en alusión al PSOE.
En este sentido, ha señalado que él tiene una "trazabilidad" y que desde que es presidente del PP, no ha aceptado que "nadie meta la mano en la caja" ni que sea "comisionista", algo que, a su juicio, no puede decir Pedro Sánchez. Por ello, ha insistido en que España necesita "un cambio político", el que representa el PP: "El cambio es imprescindible", ha defendido.
En cuanto al aborto, ha señalado que si una chica "quiere ser madre", se la va a ayudar, pero que "si después de las ayudas que se le concreten, sigue con su idea de interrumpir el embarazo, si está dentro de la ley, pues lo va a poder hacer". Respecto a las leyes LGTBI, ha indicado que actuará "exactamente igual" que con el aborto, y ha remarcado que "ese asunto está superado", aunque ha reconocido que no está conforme con la autodeterminación de género.
Sobre la ley de la eutanasia, Feijóo también ha admitido que no está de acuerdo con esa norma y quiere modificarla, por lo que podría haber "una derogación total o parcial", porque, ha señalado, "junto con la regulación de la muerte digna se tiene que garantizar una vida digna" y "todo un sistema de cuidados paliativos". Para el líder del PP, es fundamental "aseasorar bien a una persona que aparentemente toma la decisión de poner fin a su vida" y "monitorizar esos casos para ver si es una decisión irrevocable o por el contrario es una decisión en el contexto que tiene que tomarla".
Cuestionado también por el hecho de que Vox no haya condenado expresamente el franquismo, Feijóo ha recordado que el PP ya lo hizo "en la época de Aznar", y en cuanto a Abascal, ha señalado que "ha sufrido el fascismo de verdad" con ETA. "ETA es fascismo puro, que además es terrorismo, pero ETA en cuanto mata a la gente es lo más execrable de una ideología política es matar a la gente por lo que piensa", ha afirmado para decir a contiuación que existe "fascismo de derecha y de izquierda.

noticias.titulo: Sánchez asume la "responsabilidad" de sus decisiones aunque ve casos de "corrupción reales y otros ficticios"
noticias.texto:
Sánchez asume la "responsabilidad" de todas sus decisiones en el Gobierno aunque ve casos de "corrupción reales y otros ficticios"
- El candidato del PSOE a la reelección defiende la "transparencia" de las cuentas de su partido
- Comparador de programas electorales del 29N: conoce las propuestas de los partidos
El presidente del Gobierno y candidato del PSOE a la reelección, Pedro Sánchez, ha dicho que asume en primera persona "la responsabilidad" de todas las decisiones y nombramientos que ha relizado a lo largo de sus mandatos, en referencia a casos de corrupción como el que han llevado a la cárcel al exministro y exsecretario de organización del partido, José Luis Ábalos. Sin embargo, en una entrevista en Antena 3, ha apuntado a que algunos casos de corrupción "son reales" pero que otros son "ficticios".
"Soy responsable primero de todas las decisiones y de todos los nombramientos que hago como presidente del Gobierno (...) La corrupción, efectivamente, ha estado por desgracia presente en el caso de José Luis Ábalos, pero estamos hablando de un único ministro de una miriada de ministros y ministras", ha remarcado. En cambio, según él, hay otros casos que no los ve reales como las causas contra su hermano, David Sánchez; su mujer, Begoña Gómez, y también contra el exfiscal general del Estado Álvaro García Ortiz.
En el caso de su esposa, ha profundizado que antes de ser presidente ya tenía una carrera profesional consolidada y ha negado que esté involucrada en ninguna causa. Sánchez, preguntado por el expresidente José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero, ha sostenido que nunca le habló de ninguna empresas en sus conversaciones, "tampoco de Plus Ultra", en referencia a la causa abierta contra él.
Indulto al exfiscal general del Estado
Sobre García Ortiz, por cierto, ha apuntado a un posible indulto tras su condena. "Está sobre la mesa, estamos en un procedimiento y veremos exactamente cuando lo hacemos", ha sostenido Sánchez. Se trata de una decisión que tienen que tomar en el Consejo de Ministros; todavía hay algunos convocados antes de las elecciones del 29 de noviembre, y en el caso de que fuera más tarde ya lo haría el Gobierno en funciones.
En la misma entrevista, el candidato del PSOE ha defendido las cuentas de su partido y ha negado que nunca se ha financiado "irregularmente". "Tenemos una financiación absolutamente transparente", ha sostenido. "Defiendo la transparencia de mi partido, que no se ha financiado irregularmente", ha dicho, apuntando a que otras formaciones han sido condenadas por ello como el PP.
Pide esperar a las investigaciones de los accidentes de Adamuz y Urda
Preguntado por los accidentes ferroviarios de Adamuz y de Urda, con más de 100 víctimas mortales en total, Sánchez ha pedido esperar a las investigaciones que se están haciendo para esclarecer el motivo real de ambas tragedias. "Hay una autoridad independiente que se ha aprobado en mi Administración, que está haciendo una investigación absolutamente objetiva e independiente", ha explicado. Asimismo, ha dicho que "las causas del accidente de Adamuz son distintas", pero que se da la particularidad de que se han producido en la misma línea, entre Madrid y Sevila.
En el caso de Urda, Sánchez ha apuntado a fallos en el protocolo de seguridad: "Es bastante evidente que el protocolo no se siguió cuando cayó el sistema LZB en Urda y posteriormente se activó el ASFA y eso hacía que la decisión humana había llevado a que al retomar la actividad de la línea, hubiera sido el tren de delante, no el de detrás".
También ha justificado así su ausencia de la misa funeral que se celebró en la Catedral de Toledo. "En todas las tragedias, cuando ha habido pérdidas, el Gobierno ha estado presente. Cuando han tenido voluntad de hacer un funeral de Estado, he estado. Todavía no se ha logrado ese momento para celebrar esa ceremonia de Estado, pero desde el Gobierno estamos dispuestos".
Sánchez pedirá más colaboración al presidente de Gambia ante la llegada de cayucos a Canarias
En la entrevista, Pedro Sánchez también ha avanzado que a lo largo de este miércoles mantendrá una conversación con el presidente de Gambia, Adama Barrow, para pedir más colaboración de su país ante la crisis migratoria que están viviendo las islas Canarias, especialmente la isla de El Hierro. En este sentido, ha dicho que intensificará la acción diplomática también con Senegal para intentar revertir esta situación y que ambos países colaboren de una manera "más intensa".
Sobre Ceuta, el presidente del Gobierno ha defendido que la situación es "muy muy buena" respecto a la de finales de julio. "La crisis ha sido muy importante, muy severa", ha asumido, al mismo tiempo que ha cifrado en menos de 5.000 las personas migrantes que siguen a la espera de una respuesta de la administración o para ser devueltas a su país de origen.
En el caso de los menores, dice que todavía hay cerca de unos 3.500 y que son "competencia de las comunidades autónomas". "Muy probablemente es una crisis que tengamos que gestionar todas las comunidades autónomas", ha remarcado.
Confía en volver a gobernar: "No había visto jamás la movilización que estoy viviendo"
El candidato socialista a la reelección se ha mostrado "muy animado" por la campaña electoral y confía en volver a gobernar. Argumenta que aprecia una movilización que le puede favorecer. "No había visto jamás la movilización que estoy viviendo", ha dicho.
En este sentido, ha expresado que espera lograr en las elecciones del próximo 29 de noviembre "una mayoría progresista más amplia" y vuelve a repetir que u objetivo es el de lograr "176 escaños progresistas". "Si tenemos esa mayoría progresista a partir del 29 de noviembre podremos llegar antes y más lejos en materia de vivienda", ha resumido.
