noticias.titulo: No solo de la cabra vivía el majo: un estudio desvela la dieta en la antigua Fuerteventura
noticias.texto:
No solo de la cabra vivía el majo: un estudio desvela la dieta en la antigua Fuerteventura
La investigación está basada en el análisis de 8.400 huesos de animales recuperados de tres yacimientos de la Isla, que abarca diez siglos
¿De qué vivían los antiguos pobladores de Fuerteventura? La respuesta tradicional de la arqueología a esa pregunta ha sido siempre que de la carne que les proporcionaban sus rebaños de cabras, pero un nuevo estudio detallado de los yacimientos de la isla revela que no era del todo así.
Un equipo de la Universidad de Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, del Instituto de Historia del CSIC y de la empresa Arenisca, Arqueología y Patrimonio publica en 'Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports' una completa investigación sobre la alimentación de los majos, basada en el estudio de 8.400 huesos de animales recuperados de tres yacimientos de la isla, que abarca diez siglos (s. III a XIII).
Su conclusión es que los primeros pobladores de la isla más árida de Canarias combinaban el pastoreo con la pesca en la costa y la caza de aves como pardelas y codornices, de dos variedades extinguidas. Y también cazaban otros animales marinos, como la foca monje.
La estrategia de diversificar el riesgo
Es lo que apuntan los restos recuperados en tres enclaves arqueológicos muy diferentes: el costero de Punta del Mallorquín (La Oliva), el asentamiento al aire libre de Llano del Sombrero (Betancuria) y la Cueva de Villaverde (La Oliva).
"En una isla tan árida como Fuerteventura, adaptarse no significaba especializarse, sino diversificar. No poner todos los huevos en la misma cesta", resume el profesor de Prehistoria y Arqueología de la ULPGC Jonathan Santana, coordinador del proyecto científico ERC IsoCAN, en el que se inscribe este estudio.
Los yacimientos que aportan estos descubrimientos no son nuevos, ya se habían estudiado. ¿Por qué la conclusiones de este estudio son entonces diferentes? Porque las técnicas empleadas esta vez por los arqueólogos han sido distintas, mucho más finas.
La clave reside en el tamaño de los huesos de pescado, tan pequeños que suelen perderse en una excavación convencional.
En este caso, explican los autores, allí donde la tierra retirada del yacimiento se pasó por un tamiz de malla fina, como en Punta del Mallorquín, los peces suponen el 75 % de los restos. En cambio, en la zona excavada a mano, solo se recuperaron nueve restos.
"Cuando cribamos la tierra con malla fina, los restos de pescado se multiplican. La imagen de unos majos que solo vivían del ganado nos habla tanto del pasado como de la manera en que hemos excavado hasta ahora", explica Aitor Brito-Mayor (ULPGC), primer autor del estudio.
En este caso, los huesos de pescado son el 28 % de todos los restos animales recuperados de los tres yacimientos. Pertenecen a 26 especies diferentes, todas costeras, aunque con una preferencia clara: todo un emblema de la gastronomía canaria moderna como es la vieja (Sparisoma cretense) aporta el 90 % de los restos de pescado recuperados en los yacimientos de la Fuerteventura prehispánica.
Al reconstruir su tamaño a partir de los huesos, el equipo ha comprobado que durante diez siglos se pescaron de forma habitual viejas de más de 30 centímetros y alrededor de medio kilo.
El estudio ha identificado también la raíz de un colmillo de foca monje (Monachus monachus), el lobo marino que dio nombre al islote de Lobos y que hoy ha desaparecido de Canarias. Su presencia podría indicar que los majos aprovechaban este animal de forma ocasional.
Pardelas, cordornices ... ¿y un gato?
En cuanto a las aves, en los yacimientos estudiados abundan los restos de pardelas jóvenes, lo que indica que se capturaban los pollos antes de que echaran a volar.
Dos de las especies consumidas por los majos ya no existen: Una es la pardela de Olson (Puffinus olsoni), presente a lo largo de toda la secuencia, y la otra es la codorniz canaria (Coturnix gomerae), con un hueso datado que demuestra que esta ave seguía viviendo en Fuerteventura al menos hasta el siglo VII.
Los investigadores precisan, no obstante, que las aves fueron un complemento ocasional de la dieta y no una actividad especializada.
El estudio también ha deparado una sorpresa: el hallazgo de un hueso de gato en un estrato prehispánico. Los autores apuntan que podría indicar que ese animal llegó a la isla antes de la Conquista, con los primeros pobladores, pero aún esperan a datarlo directamente.
Cabras de menos de un año, guisadas y hervidas
En cuanto a la fuente principal de la alimentación aborigen en la isla, los rebaños de cabras, el estudio de los huesos recuperados.
Cerca de la mitad de las cabras eran sacrificadas en torno al año de vida, mientras que otra parte llegaba a adulta y se mantenía hasta los tres años o más. "Es la estrategia de un pastor que cuida su rebaño: se obtenía carne de los animales jóvenes, probablemente machos (los llamados tajorases), y se conservaban las hembras adultas, quizá para aprovechar su leche", precisan los autores.
Los investigadores advierten de que el presunto aprovechamiento de la leche en esa época es, por ahora, una hipótesis que tendrá que confirmarse con otros análisis, como el estudio de los restos de grasa que se conservan en las vasijas de cerámica.
Además, el 65 % de los restos de cabras y ovejas muestra huellas de fuego, con indicios de que se guisaban y se hervían para extraer la grasa. Con los cochinos se hacía algo parecido, aunque aparecen muy poco, ya que criar cerdos en un ambiente tan seco no era fácil.
El tamaño de los animales también ha sorprendido a los arqueólogos: Las cabras de los majos eran, con claridad, más robustas que las de Lanzarote, la única isla con datos comparables, procedentes del yacimiento de El Bebedero.
Las ovejas, por su parte, podrían corresponder a una oveja de pelo parecida a la actual oveja canaria de pelo (pelibuey), criada sobre todo por su carne.

noticias.titulo: Puertos Canarios impulsa nuevos servicios y espacios de sombra en el paseo marítimo de Corralejo
noticias.texto:
Puertos Canarios impulsa nuevos servicios y espacios de sombra en el paseo marítimo de Corralejo
El ente público aprueba el expediente y los pliegos para licitar una actuación de 516.325,17 euros, IGIC excluido, con un plazo de ejecución de ocho meses
Puertos Canarios ha aprobado el expediente de contratación y los pliegos que permitirán licitar las obras de construcción de casetas para la venta de tickets, aseos, vestuarios y zonas de sombra en el paseo marítimo del puerto de Corralejo, en el municipio de La Oliva, Fuerteventura.
La actuación responde a la elevada afluencia de residentes y visitantes que registra este enclave portuario y a la necesidad de reforzar los servicios disponibles para quienes transitan por el paseo marítimo, utilizan las instalaciones o participan en las actividades turísticas vinculadas al puerto.
El proyecto contempla espacios destinados a la venta y el control de tickets de excursiones, así como nuevos aseos, duchas, vestuarios y zonas de sombra. Estas dotaciones permitirán mejorar la comodidad, la accesibilidad y la atención a los usuarios, al tiempo que contribuirán a ordenar los servicios y a reforzar la calidad del entorno portuario.
El presupuesto previsto asciende a 516.325,17 euros, IGIC excluido, y el plazo de ejecución establecido en la resolución es de ocho meses. El proyecto fue redactado en diciembre de 2025 y supervisado por los servicios técnicos de Puertos Canarios, que han tramitado los informes y las aprobaciones necesarios para avanzar en su contratación.
Con esta iniciativa, Puertos Canarios continúa mejorando las infraestructuras de titularidad autonómica desde una perspectiva que combina la actividad portuaria, el servicio público y la integración de los espacios marítimos en la vida cotidiana de los municipios. La intervención busca que Corralejo disponga de un paseo marítimo más funcional, acogedor y preparado para atender las necesidades de residentes, profesionales y visitantes.
Puertos Canarios es un ente público empresarial adscrito a la Consejería de Obras Públicas, Vivienda y Movilidad del Gobierno de Canarias; que opera bajo la denominación Ecopuertos autonómicos de Canarias.

noticias.titulo: El Tritón asalta en la última jornada el liderato del Campeonato de Canarias de Barquillos de Vela Latina
noticias.texto:
El Tritón asalta en la última jornada el liderato del Campeonato de Canarias de Barquillos de Vela Latina
El barquillo de Kevin Cabrera protagoniza una gran remontada y le arrebata al Di Napoli – Isisdoro y Manuela III el título de campeón
Más emoción no se le puede pedir a la última jornada del XXXV Campeonato de Canarias de Barquillos de Vela Latina. El Di Napoli – Isidoro y Manuela III, tras dominar las primeras seis regatas de la competición, falló en las dos regatas disputadas en la mañana del domingo y de ello se aprovechó el Tritón de Kevin Cabrera para asaltar el liderato. El barquillo de Playa Blanca leyó mejor las condiciones de poco viento en el campo de regatas para proclamarse nuevo campeón de Canarias.
El Campeonato de Canarias de Barquillos de Vela Latina vivió otra mañana complicada en la jornada del domingo por la falta de viento en la bahía de Puerto del Rosario. El comienzo de la séptima regata se tuvo que retrasar hasta que aumentara la intensidad del viento, entrando rachas constantes de 5 a 6 nudos de dirección sureste y que permitió que se diera la salida a la prueba.
El Jameos del Agua de Alfredo Morales y el Romerito de David Martín se situaron al frente de la flota en la primera ceñida, pero las posiciones cambiaron en la empopada con dirección a la segunda baliza del campo de regata. La estrategia elegida permitió al Playa Dorada de Aythami Quintana y al Tritón de Kevin Cabrera situarse en los dos primeros puesto.
El viento volvió a descender en el tramo final de la regata, siendo muy complicada la navegación de los barquillos hacia la línea de meta, estando prácticamente parados. Finalmente, el Playa Dorada se apuntó la victoria, seguido de cerca por el Tritón. El Jameos del Agua se clasificó en la tercera posición, por delante del Isla de Fuerteventura de Néstor de la Nuez y del Romerito.
Una última regata de infarto
El Di Napoli – Isidoro y Manuela III afrontaba la última regata con seis puntos de ventaja sobre el Tritón, diferencia que parecía suficiente para levantar el título de campeón, pero en el mundo de la vela latina canaria todo puede suceder en el campo de regatas. La intensidad del viento volvió a aumentar para que se pudiera dar la salida a la manga.
El Tritón de Kevin Cabrera realizó una gran salida, pero una mala maniobra obligó al barquillo de Kevin Cabrera a penalizarse. Por detrás, el Di Napoli – Isidoro y Manuela III no estuvo acertado en la salida, perdiendo bastantes posiciones que le iban a costar el título de campeón. En la lucha por la victoria de la regata, el Jameos del Agua se colocó al frente de la flota por delante del Graciplus de Nete Armas.
En la penúltima boya del campo de regatas, el Tritón se colocó en la tercera posición y necesitaba meter al menos seis barcos por delante del Di Napoli – Isidoro y Manuela III para arrebatarle el liderato. El barquillo de José Pascual Perdomo se tuvo que penalizar en la última empopada, perdiendo todas las opciones de hacerse con el título de campeón.
El Jameos del Agua de Alfredo Morales se apuntó la victoria en la última regata, en la segunda posición se clasificó el Graciplus y tercero entró el Tritón. Kevin Cabrera y sus tripulantes esperaban impacientes la entrada del Di Napoli – Isidoro y Manuela III, viendo como el barquillo majorero no entraba entre los nueve primeros clasificados.
Tritón campeón de Canarias
La clasificación final del XXXV Campeonato de Canarias de Barquillos de Vela Latina dio un vuelco en la última jornada. Con un segundo y una tercera posición en las dos regatas disputadas, el Tritón de Kevin Cabrera asaltó el liderato de la competición y convierte de esa manera en el campeón de Canarias.
El Di Napoli – Isidoro y Manuela III de José Pascual Perdomo ocupó el segundo puesto de la clasificación general y el podio se completó con el tercer puesto del Jameos del Agua de Alfredo Morales. El Graciplus de Nete Armas y el Playa Blanca de Virginia Morales completan las primeras cinco posiciones de la clasificación general del XXXV Campeonato de Canarias de Barquillos de Vela Latina.
El XXXV Campeonato de Canarias de Barquillos de Vela Latina ha sido organizado por la Federación Canaria de Barquillos de Vela Latina Canaria, junto a las Federaciones Insulares de Fuerteventura, Lanzarote y Gran Canaria. Contó con la colaboración del Cabildo de Fuerteventura, Gobierno de Canarias a través de la Dirección General de Deportes Autóctonos, Ayuntamiento de Puerto del Rosario, ADI, Aguas Firgas, Puertos de Las Palmas, Radio Televisión Canaria, Aejest, Supermercados La Mar y Graciplus.

noticias.titulo: Fuerteventura se moviliza contra la agresión sufrida por un periodista canario en Madrid
noticias.texto:
Fuerteventura se moviliza contra la agresión sufrida por un periodista canario en Madrid
La concentración, convocada por un grupo de ciudadanos, tendrá lugar en Puerto del Rosario para mostrar su solidaridad con la víctima y denunciar la violencia motivada por las diferencias físicas
Puerto del Rosario acogerá una concentración ciudadana en apoyo al periodista y programador cultural canario que sufrió una agresión en Madrid el pasado viernes por motivo de su estatura. La convocatoria pretende mostrar el respaldo a la víctima y expresar el rechazo social ante este tipo de comportamientos violentos.
La movilización ha sido impulsada por un grupo de personas que ha decidido organizar una protesta pacífica, respetando la voluntad del afectado de permanecer en el anonimato. El encuentro está previsto frente a la sede de la Dirección Insular de la Administración General del Estado, en la capital majorera.
Los promotores consideran necesario dar una respuesta ciudadana ante lo sucedido y advierten de que ninguna persona debe sufrir violencia por sus características físicas. Asimismo, defienden el respeto a la diversidad y alertan de los riesgos de normalizar los discursos de odio y las actitudes discriminatorias.
El periodista fue agredido en una calle comercial de Madrid, donde un desconocido lo abordó y le propinó una patada que le provocó una fractura de fémur, mientras lo insultaba por su estatura. La Policía Nacional investiga los hechos como un posible delito de odio. Las personas convocantes animan a la ciudadanía a sumarse a la iniciativa para mostrar su solidaridad y rechazo a la violencia.

noticias.titulo: No solo de la cabra vivía el majo: un estudio desvela la dieta en la antigua Fuerteventura
noticias.texto:
No solo de la cabra vivía el majo: un estudio desvela la dieta en la antigua Fuerteventura
Un estudio arqueológico basado en 8.400 restos animales revela que los majos complementaban la ganadería de cabras con la pesca, la caza de aves y el aprovechamiento de recursos marinos
¿De qué vivían los antiguos pobladores de Fuerteventura? La respuesta tradicional de la arqueología a esa pregunta ha sido siempre que de la carne que les proporcionaban sus rebaños de cabras, pero un nuevo estudio detallado de los yacimientos de la isla revela que no era del todo así.
Un equipo de la Universidad de Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, del Instituto de Historia del CSIC y de la empresa Arenisca, Arqueología y Patrimonio publica en 'Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports' una completa investigación sobre la alimentación de los majos, basada en el estudio de 8.400 huesos de animales recuperados de tres yacimientos de la isla, que abarca diez siglos (s. III a XIII).
Su conclusión es que los primeros pobladores de la isla más árida de Canarias combinaban el pastoreo con la pesca en la costa y la caza de aves como pardelas y codornices, de dos variedades extinguidas. Y también cazaban otros animales marinos, como la foca monje.
La estrategia de diversificar el riesgo
Es lo que apuntan los restos recuperados en tres enclaves arqueológicos muy diferentes: el costero de Punta del Mallorquín (La Oliva), el asentamiento al aire libre de Llano del Sombrero (Betancuria) y la Cueva de Villaverde (La Oliva).
"En una isla tan árida como Fuerteventura, adaptarse no significaba especializarse, sino diversificar. No poner todos los huevos en la misma cesta", resume el profesor de Prehistoria y Arqueología de la ULPGC Jonathan Santana, coordinador del proyecto científico ERC IsoCAN, en el que se inscribe este estudio.
Los yacimientos que aportan estos descubrimientos no son nuevos, ya se habían estudiado. ¿Por qué la conclusiones de este estudio son entonces diferentes? Porque las técnicas empleadas esta vez por los arqueólogos han sido distintas, mucho más finas.
La clave reside en el tamaño de los huesos de pescado, tan pequeños que suelen perderse en una excavación convencional.
En este caso, explican los autores, allí donde la tierra retirada del yacimiento se pasó por un tamiz de malla fina, como en Punta del Mallorquín, los peces suponen el 75 % de los restos. En cambio, en la zona excavada a mano, solo se recuperaron nueve restos.
"Cuando cribamos la tierra con malla fina, los restos de pescado se multiplican. La imagen de unos majos que solo vivían del ganado nos habla tanto del pasado como de la manera en que hemos excavado hasta ahora", explica Aitor Brito-Mayor (ULPGC), primer autor del estudio.
En este caso, los huesos de pescado son el 28 % de todos los restos animales recuperados de los tres yacimientos. Pertenecen a 26 especies diferentes, todas costeras, aunque con una preferencia clara: todo un emblema de la gastronomía canaria moderna como es la vieja (Sparisoma cretense) aporta el 90 % de los restos de pescado recuperados en los yacimientos de la Fuerteventura prehispánica.
Al reconstruir su tamaño a partir de los huesos, el equipo ha comprobado que durante diez siglos se pescaron de forma habitual viejas de más de 30 centímetros y alrededor de medio kilo.
El estudio ha identificado también la raíz de un colmillo de foca monje (Monachus monachus), el lobo marino que dio nombre al islote de Lobos y que hoy ha desaparecido de Canarias. Su presencia podría indicar que los majos aprovechaban este animal de forma ocasional.
Pardelas, cordornices ... ¿y un gato?
En cuanto a las aves, en los yacimientos estudiados abundan los restos de pardelas jóvenes, lo que indica que se capturaban los pollos antes de que echaran a volar.
Dos de las especies consumidas por los majos ya no existen: Una es la pardela de Olson (Puffinus olsoni), presente a lo largo de toda la secuencia, y la otra es la codorniz canaria (Coturnix gomerae), con un hueso datado que demuestra que esta ave seguía viviendo en Fuerteventura al menos hasta el siglo VII.
Los investigadores precisan, no obstante, que las aves fueron un complemento ocasional de la dieta y no una actividad especializada.
El estudio también ha deparado una sorpresa: el hallazgo de un hueso de gato en un estrato prehispánico. Los autores apuntan que podría indicar que ese animal llegó a la isla antes de la Conquista, con los primeros pobladores, pero aún esperan a datarlo directamente.
Cabras de menos de un año, guisadas y hervidas
En cuanto a la fuente principal de la alimentación aborigen en la isla, los rebaños de cabras, el estudio de los huesos recuperados.
Cerca de la mitad de las cabras eran sacrificadas en torno al año de vida, mientras que otra parte llegaba a adulta y se mantenía hasta los tres años o más. "Es la estrategia de un pastor que cuida su rebaño: se obtenía carne de los animales jóvenes, probablemente machos (los llamados tajorases), y se conservaban las hembras adultas, quizá para aprovechar su leche", precisan los autores.
Los investigadores advierten de que el presunto aprovechamiento de la leche en esa época es, por ahora, una hipótesis que tendrá que confirmarse con otros análisis, como el estudio de los restos de grasa que se conservan en las vasijas de cerámica.
Además, el 65 % de los restos de cabras y ovejas muestra huellas de fuego, con indicios de que se guisaban y se hervían para extraer la grasa. Con los cochinos se hacía algo parecido, aunque aparecen muy poco, ya que criar cerdos en un ambiente tan seco no era fácil.
El tamaño de los animales también ha sorprendido a los arqueólogos: Las cabras de los majos eran, con claridad, más robustas que las de Lanzarote, la única isla con datos comparables, procedentes del yacimiento de El Bebedero.
Las ovejas, por su parte, podrían corresponder a una oveja de pelo parecida a la actual oveja canaria de pelo (pelibuey), criada sobre todo por su carne.

noticias.titulo: El Consorcio de Aguas de Fuerteventura aprueba un presupuesto de 25,36 millones de euros para 2027
noticias.texto:
El Consorcio de Aguas de Fuerteventura aprueba un presupuesto de 25,36 millones de euros para 2027
Las cuentas aumentan más de un 10 % y permitirán continuar con la modernización de las desaladoras y las redes de distribución de agua.
El Consorcio de Abastecimiento de Aguas a Fuerteventura (CAAF) ha aprobado su presupuesto general para 2027, que asciende a 25,36 millones de euros, lo que supone un incremento de más de un 10% respecto a este año, según ha informado el Cabildo en un comunicado.
La presidenta de la corporación insular, Lola García, destaca que este presupuesto les facilita continuar con la línea de trabajo que han venido desarrollando "para mejorar y garantizar la prestación de este servicio público".
"Estas cuentas nos permiten seguir realizando inversiones para la renovación y ampliación de las plantas desaladoras y redes de distribución, garantizando los caudales necesarios a la población", apunta.
El consejero de Aguas, Adargoma Hernández, señala que "las previsiones presupuestarias del CAAF continúan condicionadas por el contexto económico global que afecta a su principal coste de producción: la energía eléctrica, así como a las necesidades de abastecimiento que requieren las empresas y familias de Fuerteventura".
En este sentido, Hernández resalta las inversiones para mejorar las redes, las plantas desaladoras y sistemas de gestión, a financiar con recursos propios y con fondos procedentes del Fdcan ya autorizados.
Tanto la presidenta Lola García como Adargoma Hernández han agradecido el esfuerzo realizado por el personal del Cabildo y los ayuntamientos como entes consorciados.

noticias.titulo: El Área de Salud de Fuerteventura desarrolla una campaña para prevenir y detectar precozmente la diabetes
noticias.texto:
El Área de Salud de Fuerteventura desarrolla una campaña para prevenir y detectar precozmente la diabetes
La iniciativa incluyó controles de glucemia en Morro Jable y actividades informativas en todos los centros de salud, además de acciones para prevenir las complicaciones del pie diabético
El Área de Salud de Fuerteventura ha llevado a cabo una campaña de concienciación sobre la diabetes con motivo de su Día Mundial, con el objetivo de acercar a la población información sobre la prevención, la detección temprana y los cuidados necesarios para evitar complicaciones asociadas a esta enfermedad.
La iniciativa, promovida por la Red de Promoción de la Salud de Atención Primaria (REDPSAP), incluyó una jornada informativa en la Plaza de los Pescadores de Morro Jable, además de la instalación de mesas de sensibilización en todos los centros de salud de la isla. La actividad desarrollada en el municipio de Pájara contó con la colaboración del Ayuntamiento y de la Asociación Majorera para la Diabetes (AMADI).
Durante la jornada se realizaron más de un centenar de controles de glucemia y se ofreció asesoramiento sobre hábitos saludables, alimentación equilibrada y actividad física. Los profesionales sanitarios incidieron especialmente en la importancia de identificar los factores de riesgo, ya que la diabetes tipo 2 puede permanecer durante años sin manifestar síntomas evidentes.
La campaña también sirvió para dar a conocer el trabajo que desarrolla el personal de enfermería a través del programa BPSO, una iniciativa que promueve la aplicación de recomendaciones basadas en la evidencia científica para mejorar la atención sanitaria.
En este marco, el Área de Salud cuenta con la guía 'Disminución de las complicaciones del pie en personas con diabetes', centrada en prevenir lesiones y mejorar los cuidados. Entre sus recomendaciones figuran revisar los pies de forma periódica, mantener una higiene e hidratación adecuadas, utilizar calzado apropiado y acudir a los profesionales sanitarios ante cualquier herida, cambio de coloración o pérdida de sensibilidad.

noticias.titulo: Sánchez pedirá hoy más colaboración al presidente de Gambia ante la crisis migratoria
noticias.texto:
Sánchez pedirá hoy más colaboración al presidente de Gambia ante la crisis migratoria
El Gobierno busca intensificar la cooperación diplomática con Senegal y Gambia para frenar el repunte de llegadas de cayucos a Canarias, especialmente a El Hierro.
El jefe del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, mantendrá este miércoles una conversación con el presidente de Gambia, Adama Barrow, para pedir más colaboración de su país ante la crisis de inmigración irregular que está afectando especialmente a la isla de El Hierro.
Sánchez ha avanzado que mantendrá ese diálogo telefónico, en una entrevista en Antena 3 en la que ha asegurado que el Ejecutivo está llevando a cabo una acción diplomática tanto con Senegal como con Gambia (países de origen de los cayucos que llegan a las costas canarias) para intentar frenar esta situación.
Ha asegurado que esos dos países están colaborando, pero ha subrayado que se necesita que esa cooperación sea más intensa.
Sánchez ha destacado la acción humanitaria que se ha dado ante este "pico" de llegadas y se ha dirigido a los ciudadanos de Canarias para garantizarles que se están desplegando todas las capacidades del Estado con el fin de hacer frente a lo que está ocurriendo.

noticias.titulo: Senegal detiene a 46 emigrantes indocumentados y a cuatro traficantes de personas en pleno repunte de llegadas a Canarias
noticias.texto:
Senegal detiene a 46 emigrantes indocumentados y a cuatro traficantes de personas en pleno repunte de llegadas a Canarias
Las operaciones en Dakar coinciden con el aumento de la presión migratoria en la ruta atlántica, donde la Armada senegalesa ha rescatado a más de 1.700 personas en las últimas dos semanas.
Las autoridades de Senegal han detenido a 46 personas que pretendían emigrar de forma irregular y a cuatro presuntos traficantes de personas en dos operaciones desarrolladas en Dakar, en un contexto marcado por el repunte de llegadas de cayucos a Canarias durante las últimas semanas.
Según ha informado este miércoles la Gendarmería Nacional senegalesa, la primera intervención tuvo lugar el pasado 16 de noviembre en el distrito pesquero de Yoff Ndenatte, donde fueron interceptados 15 migrantes, entre ellos tres mujeres, y un supuesto traficante. Durante la operación, los agentes se incautaron de un motor de embarcación, documentos de identidad, un GPS y dinero en efectivo.
La segunda actuación se produjo este martes en Toubab Dialaw, una localidad costera situada al sur de Dakar, donde las autoridades detuvieron a otras 34 personas, entre ellas tres presuntos traficantes. Los agentes confiscaron también un motor de 40 caballos de potencia, un GPS, una brújula y provisiones.
Estas operaciones coinciden con un incremento de la actividad migratoria en la ruta atlántica hacia Canarias, especialmente en El Hierro. Solo el pasado sábado, el archipiélago recibió a 1.580 migrantes a bordo de quince cayucos, en la jornada con mayor número de rescates en los 32 años de historia de esta ruta.
Senegal constituye uno de los principales países de origen y tránsito de las personas que intentan alcanzar las costas canarias. Durante las últimas dos semanas, la Armada senegalesa ha rescatado a más de 1.700 personas que trataban de emigrar de manera irregular.
La ruta atlántica continúa siendo una de las más peligrosas del mundo. Según los datos de la Organización Internacional para las Migraciones (OIM), al menos 454 personas han fallecido o desaparecido durante estas travesías desde principios de 2026.
Ante el incremento de llegadas al archipiélago, el ministro del Interior, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, solicitó el pasado 6 de noviembre a las autoridades senegalesas reforzar la cooperación en materia migratoria durante una visita oficial a Dakar.
El Gobierno español busca intensificar la colaboración con los países de origen para prevenir las salidas de embarcaciones y combatir las redes de tráfico de personas que operan en la ruta migratoria hacia Canarias.

noticias.titulo: Iberia Express ofrecerá wifi gratuito de alta velocidad en sus vuelos a Canarias
noticias.texto:
Iberia Express ofrecerá wifi gratuito de alta velocidad en sus vuelos a Canarias
La aerolínea será la primera compañía de bajo coste en incorporar la tecnología Starlink en las rutas entre Madrid y el archipiélago, con velocidades de hasta 500 Mbps.
Iberia Express ofrecerá conexión gratuita a internet de alta velocidad a bordo de sus vuelos entre Madrid y Canarias gracias a la incorporación de la tecnología satelital Starlink. La compañía comenzará en los próximos días la adaptación de su primer avión para implantar este servicio, que estará disponible para todos los pasajeros, independientemente de la clase en la que viajen.
La aerolínea tiene previsto equipar durante los próximos dos meses un total de 16 aviones de su flota, pertenecientes a los modelos Airbus A321neo y A320ceo, con el objetivo de extender progresivamente esta tecnología a la totalidad de sus aeronaves.
La conexión, que permitirá alcanzar velocidades de hasta 500 Mbps, ofrecerá a los pasajeros la posibilidad de acceder a plataformas de streaming, seguir competiciones deportivas en directo, descargar contenidos audiovisuales, consultar las redes sociales y utilizar otros servicios de internet durante el trayecto.
La directora comercial de Iberia Express, Isabel Rodríguez, ha destacado que la incorporación de Starlink supondrá una mejora significativa en la experiencia de los pasajeros y ha subrayado la importancia de estrenar este servicio en las conexiones con Canarias.
Con esta iniciativa, Iberia Express se convertirá en la primera aerolínea de bajo coste en ofrecer esta tecnología en las rutas que conectan la capital española con el archipiélago.
La compañía, perteneciente al Grupo Iberia, cuenta actualmente con una flota de 21 aeronaves y mantiene una destacada presencia en las conexiones entre Madrid, Canarias y Baleares.
Según los datos de la consultora Cirium, Iberia Express fue la aerolínea más puntual de Europa en 2025 por tercer año consecutivo, mientras que en 2026 se ha situado como la tercera mejor compañía de bajo coste de Europa y la quinta del mundo, según el ranking de Skytrax.

noticias.titulo: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war with Russia
noticias.resumen: Watch: The BBC's Jonathan Beale joins Ukrainian forces taking the battle below ground and out of sight of Russian drones.
noticias.texto:
Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war with Russia
For the past seven months Ukrainian forces have been living and fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet gas pipeline in the Kharkiv region.
The BBC is the first international broadcaster to enter the pipeline where this subterranean battle is taking place.
With a diameter of just over a metre there's enough room only to crawl. But it is relatively safe from the drones that now saturate the skies above the front line â and which are making it nigh-on impossible for either side to advance.
The BBC's defence correspondent Jonathan Beale reports from near Kupyansk, where he went underground with the 13th Khartiia Operational Brigade.

noticias.titulo: 'The drones don't fly here' - BBC reports from Ukraine's new front line
noticias.resumen: Ukrainian forces are fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet tunnel in the Kharkiv region.
noticias.texto:
Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war
- Published
There's a new front in the war in Ukraine, and it is underground.
For the past seven months Ukrainian forces have been living and fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet gas pipeline in the north-eastern Kharkiv region.
With a diameter of just over a metre there is enough room only to crawl. But it is relatively safe from the drones that now saturate the skies above the front line â and make it nigh-on impossible for either side to advance.
Going underground is now the "only option", says Zanuda, who has helped plan Ukraine's tunnel operation and calls it a new world of fighting. But, he acknowledges, it is hard.
"On the surface you always have some room to manoeuvre, but here you can only engage the enemy head-on."
The journey to get to this subterranean battleground in the Kharkiv region only reinforced the dangers on the ground: a high-speed move by vehicle across open fields, followed by a long march across muddy ground â accompanied by Ukrainian troops with their weapons loaded, ready to shoot down Russian drones.
Arriving at the tunnel entrance, the first thing to hit you is the lingering smell of gas and fetid air.
Both sides use openings in the pipeline to get to the surface, where most of the fighting takes place. They have made breaches in the ground, and used welding tools to break through the thick steel.
The Russians were the first to exploit the pipe to infiltrate the nearby city of Kupyansk in September 2025. They have used underground pipelines before, during the capture of the city of Avdiivka in 2024, and last year in their bid to recapture areas of Russia's Kursk region.
But Ukrainian forces have slowly turned the tables.
A specially designed electric cart transports troops and supplies through the pipeline.
They call it the Kupyansk metro. It occasionally breaks down. We travelled on it for 40 minutes, heads bowed and legs crossed. There is a regular bump as you cross the welded sections of the pipe. It is like an austere fairground ride, without the fun.
Our destination was a break in the pipeline where Ukrainian troops have built dug-outs to store ammunition and equipment, with just enough room to stand. It is where the man they call Musician conducts the movement of troops and supplies. He has been living like a mole, his face engrained with dirt and earth.
Musician tells me he has spent the past three months there, with a few brief visits above ground to clean up or go to the toilet. From time to time we can hear the thuds of artillery rounds above. Musician tells me we are close to the line of contact: "But it's safe underground."
The cart continues its journey into the bowels of the earth. It returns about half an hour later with more troops covered in dirt. They have been fighting in positions on the surface.
There is a look of relief on their dust-caked faces.
"It's more comfortable in the pipe because drones don't fly here, and neither do artillery shells or glide bombs," says Vovochka, who has been fighting on the ground for the past three weeks.
But there has been fighting in the pipeline, too. Operation Veles, named after a mythical Slavic god of the underworld, began in April. Since then Ukraine has advanced 15km (9.3 miles) along the pipeline.
It has been painstaking, backbreaking work â with the ever-present fear of coming into contact with the enemy.
Back above ground we meet a few of the soldiers, from the 13th Khartiia Brigade of Ukraine's National Guard, who have taken part in the mission. Their first task was to clear the detritus, water and Russian barricades inside the pipeline.
The Ukrainian troops say some of the barriers were boobytrapped or piled with Russian bodies. "When we moved them or climbed over them, we had no idea what was underneath," says Chyzh.
The other danger, he said, was the ricochets from gunfire when they tried to advance. "You never know where a bullet is going to go or how it will bounce."
His comrade Kort says "we were all firing, we were pushing them back". Over the course of the operation Ukraine says it killed more than 100 Russian soldiers and took 30 prisoners. "Yes, there were bodies," says Kort. "I even had to sleep right next to them."
Their commander's former life as a miner helped prepare them for the physical and psychological challenges of operating underground.
From a building on the surface, Biashym keeps in regular contact with his men still in the pipeline. Behind him is a cabinet full of medicine.
Soldiers in the pipeline spend much of their time on their knees and suffer abrasions. Biashym admits some have had panic attacks from living in such a confined space. Others have struggled to breathe.
Hundreds of Colombian volunteers have also been involved in the operation, part of the RUG 23rd Assault Regiment.
Foreign fighters have helped boost Ukraine's depleted ranks. One of the Colombians, whose call sign is Gecko, tells me it took them 30 days to just clear 500m.
"It was difficult, it was hot and I had fear inside the pipe," he said. "But at some point I just thought, OK, just deal with it and let's advance."
The battle of the pipeline is not over.
Russian forces, like Ukraine's, have built fortified positions inside the pipeline. They still try to infiltrate Ukrainian positions, burrowing their way in and out of the pipe. From a control room above ground we watched Ukrainian drones target another Russian attempt to outflank them.
Ground operations are now nearly impossible... everyone understands, for now, the only way to fight is underground
While some of the fighting taking place underground, there are still battles on the surface and in the air. It has been a combined operation.
But Zanuda, who is chief of the planning section of the 13th Khartiia Brigade, believes it is the best way to fight in the future. "Ground operations are now nearly impossible," he said, adding that "everyone understands, for now, the only way to fight is underground".
There'll be more missions like this, he believes. "Pipelines run everywhere," he said. "You have to remember, back in the Soviet times, oil, gas and ammonia were being transported to Europe, with the entire transit route running through Ukraine."
In reality it has been brutal, gruelling and dangerous work in the harshest of conditions.
It has taken Ukraine seven months to clear 15km of the pipeline.
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has hailed it as a success.
It has helped retake lost territory and been a boost for morale, but on its own it has not changed the course of the war.
Additional reporting by Moose Campbell, Volodymyr Lozhko and Rebecca Hartmann

noticias.titulo: Trump shakes hands with Putin and Xi ahead of historic talks in China
noticias.resumen: The three leaders will meet together for the first time on Thursday during a closely-watched summit.
noticias.texto:
Trump shakes hands with Putin and Xi ahead of historic talks in China
- Published
Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met for the first time in more than a year on Wednesday, as they prepared for landmark talks in China with Xi Jinping.
The US president was greeted off his plane by the Chinese leader as he arrived in Shenzhen for a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders, which will culminate in a closely-watched meeting between the pair and the Russian president.
After a carefully choreographed handshake and hug between Trump and Xi on the tarmac, the US president later greeted and exchanged pleasantries with Putin ahead of a reception.
Trump and Putin are expected to hold one-on-one talks on the sidelines of the summit on Thursday, in which the war in Ukraine could be discussed.
However the main focus during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum (Apec) will be on the US-China-Russia talks on Thursday - the first time the trio of leaders have met together in person.
A full agenda has not been made public but there have been various hints about what could be discussed, including the wars in Ukraine and Iran, nuclear proliferation, trade tensions and developments in artificial intelligence.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Putin and Trump have not yet held a substantive meeting, and merely greeted each other on Wednesday.
Peskov also said that "no more than an hour" had been allocated for Thursday's trilateral talks between Putin, Trump and Xi.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has raised fears of a plan to end the war being discussed in the absence of representatives from Kyiv or Europe.
It is unclear whether China would want this issue to be on the agenda in Shenzhen, with Beijing talking more generally about the need to discuss "safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability".
China has officially remained neutral since Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, rejecting accusations from Kyiv and its allies that it has been tacitly supporting Moscow, including by exporting dual-use technology used by the Russian military.
Wednesday's handshake was the first in-person meeting between Trump and Putin since August 2025, when the Russian leader travelled to Alaska for talks on the Ukraine war which failed to deliver a breakthrough.
Xi's personal reception for Trump at the airport mimicked a similar move by the US president when the Chinese leader visited Washington in September, a gesture Xi described as "special".
In Shenzhen, a red carpet was rolled out in front of Air Force One for Trump, with a cheering crowd, honour guard, military flyover and flowers presentation all in place to welcome him.
Chinese state-run news agency Xinhua quoted Xi as saying he wanted to pursue a "constructive strategic and stable relationship based on respect, fairness, and equality".
Xi's greeting will be seen as a diplomatic gesture designed to begin the week's talks with his American counterpart on a cordial note.
The south-east Chinese city the Apec summit is being held in is a booming area for manufacturing and advanced tech.
It comes against the backdrop of the ousting of Nvidia chief executing Jensen Huang, who admitted to having an affair with a woman suspected by US intelligence of spying for Beijing - a claim dismissed as a "smear" by China.
Trump has pursued warmer relations with China but the incident points to ongoing tensions between the two powers.
Several hours before Trump's arrival, Putin landed in Shenzhen and held around two hours of talks with Xi, with whom he has pressed for closer economic and defence relations.
Xi said both countries would "move forward steadily and boldly" and that the relationship was "stable as a mountain, unshaken by storms".

noticias.titulo: Israeli military launches rare ground operation in Gaza beyond Yellow Line
noticias.resumen: Hamas condemns the incursion, which the Israeli military says is dismantling a "terror tunnel", as a "flagrant" ceasefire violation.
noticias.texto:
Israeli military launches rare ground operation in Gaza beyond Yellow Line
- Published
Israeli ground forces have launched a rare operation in part of the central Gaza Strip outside their control, after issuing evacuation orders for residents.
Witnesses said tanks advanced east of Nuseirat refugee camp and rolled onto the territory's main north to south road under the cover of artillery strikes.
The Israeli military said the "targeted" operation aimed to dismantle a "terror tunnel" west of the so-called Yellow Line, which marks the more than 60% of Gaza's territory occupied by Israel.
The Palestinian armed group Hamas, which controls the rest of Gaza, accused Israel of a "flagrant violation" of the October 2025 ceasefire agreement.
Violence has continued in Gaza over the past 13 months, with near-daily Israeli strikes, and living conditions for the 2.1 million people there remain dire.
Early on Wednesday afternoon, Israeli military body Cogat's Arabic spokesperson announced the start of the incursion and warned Palestinians living in an area north of Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camp to stay away for their own safety.
It also said a section of the north to south Salah al-Din road that passed through the area would be closed to traffic.
Later, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said it had begun a joint operation with the Shin Bet security service "to dismantle a terror tunnel west of the Yellow Line that posed an immediate and direct threat to IDF troops".
"IDF troops under the Southern Command are deployed in the area in accordance with the ceasefire agreement and will continue to operate to remove any immediate threat and thwart attempts by the Hamas terrorist organisation to harm Israeli civilians or IDF troops, or to violate the agreement," it added.
Hamas warned in a statement that the advance of Israeli military vehicles beyond the Yellow Line and the evacuation of residents constituted "a dangerous development and a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement".
Footage published by Palestinian media outlets and on social media showed families fleeing areas near Nuseirat camp following the announcement.
In one video verified by BBC Verify, a man can be seen ducking after hearing artillery fire and then running along Salah al-Din road, about 1.5km (0.9 miles) west of the Yellow Line. "The Israeli occupation now is firing randomly near the houses and tents of people," he says.
Automatic gunfire can be heard in another video filmed just to the south-east.
A resident of Nuseirat who was forced to flee told BBC Arabic's Middle East Daily programme: "The situation is now extremely dire, with Israeli forces firing indiscriminately at areas where displaced people have sought shelter."
"We couldn't take any of our belongings with us - not even our blankets, pillows, or clothes. We had no choice but to leave everything behind."
A second resident also reported "indiscriminate gunfire and shelling" and said there had been "numerous casualties, including fatalities".
Asked about reported fatalities, the IDF sent a general statement about the operation.
Gaza's Hamas-run Civil Defence agency said three people were killed and others were wounded in three separate Israeli drone strikes on Wednesday.
One man was killed in Nuseirat, the second to the north in Gaza City, and the third in the central town of Deir al-Balah, it added.
The Israeli military said the first two strikes targeted "terrorists" and that it was not aware of the third incident, according to AFP news agency.
At least 1,658 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since the ceasefire began last year, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
The Israeli military says six of its soldiers have been killed over the same period.
Meanwhile, more than 1.9 million people - about 90% of Gaza's population - remain displaced, with 1.4 million of them living in tents or makeshift shelters, according to the UN.
Reconstruction has yet to begin in Gaza, where an estimated 82% of all structures have been destroyed or damaged during the war, as US President Donald Trump's peace plan has largely stalled.
The disarmament of Hamas has been a key sticking point.
The group has agreed to give up its weapons in exchange for a phased withdrawal of Israeli troops from the 60% of Gaza they currently occupy. But Israel has insisted that Hamas must fully disarm before any pullout.
The war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.
Since then, more than 74,700 people have been killed in Gaza, the health ministry says.

noticias.titulo: William and Kate meet PM Modi as they wrap up India tour
noticias.resumen: The meeting in New Delhi was a late addition to the royal couple's India visit, which also included their appearance at the annual Earthshot Prize
noticias.texto:
William and Kate meet PM Modi as they wrap up India tour
- Published
The Prince and Princess of Wales have met India's prime minister as they ended their three-day visit to the country.
Narendra Modi thanked Prince William for bringing his Earthshot prize to the country during the couple's first international tour since 2022.
It comes a day after the royal couple gave out Â£1m prizes to winners of the environmental award, which was founded by the prince and remains one of his biggest personal projects.
Catherine also visited a maternity hospital, where she comforted a grieving mother who lost a baby after giving birth to premature twin girls.
On Wednesday, William and Catherine travelled from Mumbai to capital New Delhi for the final leg of their trip.
During a meeting at Modi's private residence, a Kensington Palace spokesperson said the royals and Modi discussed the "strength and importance of the UKâIndia bilateral relationship, reflecting on the deep and enduring ties between the two countries and the opportunities to strengthen their partnership in the years ahead".
The prince and princess also spoke "warmly" of their time in the country, thanking the prime minister and the people for their welcome, and saying how much they enjoyed returning to India, a decade after their last visit.
Modi called it a "pleasure" to meet them, and said he looks forward to "further strengthening" the UKâIndia partnership for the "shared prosperity of the people of our nations and the wider world".
When Prince William announced earlier this year that The Earthshot Prize ceremony was going to be held in India for the first time, he highlighted India's leadership in climate innovation, its biodiversity and its massive youth population as the key reasons for choosing the country.
The royal spokesperson said that the meeting with Modi touched on the success of the ceremony in Mumbai, and India's "growing leadership in environmental innovation".
The event, founded by Prince William in 2020, was hosted this year by Karan Johar, presenter of The Traitors India and one of the country's most well-known filmmakers.
The couple last met the Indian prime minister on their official visit to India in 2016.
Ahead of their meeting with Modi on Wednesday, William met with film stars during a visit to a film production company, while Catherine visited a maternity hospital, where she met grieving mother Jyoti Karande.
Karande, whose other child remains in intensive care, is receiving treatment in the post-partum ward at Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital.
Catherine told the 29-year-old: "Stay strong. Well done. You've clearly been very, very brave."
William and Catherine's first official overseas trip in four years was short, but allowed them to combine personal projects - like Earthshot - with diplomacy.
As the future king and queen, they are viewed as a valuable diplomatic asset by the UK government.
And with Catherine recovering well and back on international duties following her cancer treatment, visits of a similar kind can be expected to fill their calendar.

noticias.titulo: Kuwait says it repelled first Iranian attack in two months after US strikes island
noticias.resumen: Bahrain says it was also attacked by Iran following a US air strike on the Iranian island of Qeshm in the Gulf on Tuesday.
noticias.texto:
Kuwait says it repelled first Iranian attack in two months after US strikes island
- Published
Kuwait and Bahrain have said they repelled Iranian air attacks overnight as hostilities between Iran and the United States rise.
The drone attack on Kuwait was the first in more than two months. The Iranian army said it had targeted the Ali Al Salem Airbase, which hosts US forces, but Kuwaiti authorities did not report any damage.
It came after US warplanes struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, according to US military officials.
Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates' state oil firm said a crew member was missing after one of its tankers was attacked in the Gulf waterway on Tuesday.
The recent exchanges of fire, as well as deadlock in negotiations on a peace deal, have raised fears of a major escalation in the nine-month-old war.
The conflict began when the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February.
Since then, Iran has retaliated for US and Israeli strikes by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel.
It has also attacked dozens of commercial vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass.
- Pakistani man sentenced to 27 years for Iran-backed plot to kill Trump 
  - Published18 hours ago
- Iran targets US military base in Bahrain with drone attack 
  - Published3 days ago
On Tuesday night, Kuwait's military said its air defences engaged "drone threats" but did not report any casualties or damage.
The Kuwaiti foreign ministry condemned the attack, saying it "flagrantly violated Kuwait's sovereignty, directly threatened its security and stability, and constituted a grave breach of international law".
"The explosions seemed to be coming from far away, but hearing them again after a period of calm was both surprising and worrying," Hani Mohammed, an Egyptian resident of Kuwait, told AFP news agency.
Bahrain's military also said on Wednesday that its air defence systems had "intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks".
The island kingdom, which hosts the US Navy's 5th Fleet, has reported four attacks over the past six days, following a two-month lull.
Qatar, which has mediated in the stalled indirect talks between Iran and the US, said the Iranian attacks on its neighbours were a "dangerous escalation that threatens to complicate efforts aimed at containing tensions".
The Iranian army said its drones had targeted US Patriot air defence systems and drone and missile launch platforms at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait.
Later, the army's commander-in-chief, Maj Gen Amir Hatami, warned the US and its allies that it would respond more forcefully to any new attacks on Iran.
"If the enemy repeats its mistake... we have the readiness and the plans to confront it and its supporters in a stronger, more crushing way and without geographic limitations," he said.
On Tuesday night, US fighter jets targeted a missile launch site on Qeshm Island "with precision munitions" in response to Iranian "aggression targeting US personnel and assets", US military officials said.
Iranian media reported explosions on the island but cited a local official as saying they had caused no damage to infrastructure.
In a separate development, the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (Adnoc) said a search-and-rescue operation was under way for a missing sailor following an attack on one of its vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday. The rest of the crew were safely evacuated and 11 were receiving medical care, it added.
The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) centre reported that a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile about 13 nautical miles (24km) north of Khasab, in Oman's Musandam peninsula. It said the attack caused a fire on board that was extinguished.
Iran said two oil tankers and a ship carrying liquefied natural gas (LNG) had caught fire after hitting naval mines while sailing along an "authorised route".
At least 25 seafarers have been killed across the Middle East since the start of the war, when the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed due to Iranian missile and drone attacks on commercial vessels and a US naval blockade of Iranian ports.
The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the conflict and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.
Iran insisted it would not give up some measure of control over the waterway and began targeting vessels using a southern route through Omani waters that avoids its preferred route through Iranian waters.
In recent months, the US military has been providing protection for tankers shuttling through the Strait of Hormuz, allowing crude oil exports from Gulf states to reach around 80% of pre-war levels, according to analysts.

noticias.titulo: Grand Theft Auto 6 is a masterpiece, say critics
noticias.resumen: Critics have their say as to whether GTA 6, the most anticipated video game of all time, lives up to the hype.
noticias.texto:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is a masterpiece, say critics
- Published
After 13 years of waiting, record-breaking trailers and lengthy delays, critics have given their answer to one of the year's biggest questions.
Does Grand Theft Auto 6, surely the most anticipated game of all time, live up to the hype?
According to the first reviews, it's a resounding yes.
Metacritic, which aggregates reviews from critics, averages it at 99 out of 100, external - tying with Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has held the record since 1998.
Reviewers overwhelmingly agreed the open-world action game was an ambitious, ground-breaking title that was well worth the wait.
Not everyone is enjoying the glowing praise - with some posters to online forums objecting to what one called "the ultra fan-boy hype."
But there is no question the reviewers have been effusive with their praise, with gaming website IGN, external branding GTA 6 "unprecedented", "unbelievable" and "unmissable".
Meanwhile in its five star review, Eurogamer said makers Rockstar had "pushed back the horizon of video games once again" with its graphics, storytelling and world building.
"The awe is all part of the point, of course, and GTA 6 is nothing if not truly awesome," reviewer Chris Tapsell wrote, external, but he added "there are also nits to pick".
For The New York Times, external one of those nits was whether the realism of the game might dull the fun chaos of its predecessors.
Reviewer Yussef Cole said GTA 6 had "matured beyond its memorable car crashes and stickups" with consequences to every action.
But "some of my favourite moments have been careening through streets with squad cars in hot pursuit," he wrote.
The graphics of the game were hotly anticipated and so far have not disappointed critics, with The Guardian, external describing Leonida, the setting inspired by Miami, as "so lifelike that at times it beggars belief".
And the relationship between the lead characters, Jason and Lucia, has also stunned critics.
"They feel like real people rather than puppets dancing to your whim," The Guardian's Keza MacDonald wrote, adding: "I found it impossible not to care for them".
Writing for Forbes, external, Paul Tassi said: "I can't say I've ever seen a better video game relationship than the one they share".
The Washington Post, external said GTA 6 "raises the bar at every level", while Bloomberg, external's Jason Schreier called it a "masterpiece" in his five star review.
"It's hard not to be astonished by what Rockstar has done here," he wrote. "There's nothing else like it.
"While playing this game, I often found myself wondering how it even exists."
Rockstar hasn't revealed the cost of the game, but some estimates put the figure north of $1bn (Â£760m).
Gaming journalist Jordan Middler is one of the lucky few in the UK who got early access from Rockstar and tells BBC Newsbeat it is the "game of a generation".
He'd played for about 100 hours by the time he hit the credits and says he still has so much to do.
Middler did spot one negative though - he found the game can "slow down" because of how much is going on.
He also says it is "long overdue" that there is a female lead in Lucia.
"The way previous GTA games have dealt with women has been a boys' club approach," he says.
"Introducing Lucia and not making her some kind of token character, she just fits in completely... and she will quickly become a fan favourite without question."
Early nominations
The Game Awards - the most watched ceremony of its kind in the industry - gave players a teaser of the critical reception when its 2026 nominations were revealed on Tuesday.
And despite having not released at the time, GTA 6 was the most-nominated title.
It will be up for eight prizes, including game of the year and best music.
The nomination of Manni L Perez in the best performance category confirmed wide speculation that she is the actress behind main character Lucia in GTA 6 - a fact Rockstar hadn't previously officially confirmed.
The jury for the event is largely made up of gaming journalists around the world, who would have received advanced copies for review.
Some, though, have questioned how a game that has just been released has garnered such positive reviews and award nominations.
There is a view in some online forums that the hype around the game has got out of control as, with one poster commenting: "I think everyone's tired of hearing about this game - I don't even want to play it anymore."
It appears so far, however, that is likely to be very much a minority view.
Additional reporting by Jasmine Sandhar

noticias.titulo: Parents jailed for torture and death of four-year-old girl found along French motorway in 1987
noticias.resumen: Inass Touloub's body was found along the A10 road in 1987, bearing marks of abuse, and was not identified until 2018.
noticias.texto:
Parents jailed for torture and death of four-year-old girl in France in 1987
- Published
The mother of a four-year-old girl killed in central France and found along a motorway almost 40 years ago has been sentenced to 20 years in prison.
Halima El Bakhti, 72, was found guilty on Tuesday of "torture and acts of barbarity resulting in death without the intent to kill", French media reports.
The girl's father, 74-year-old Ahmed Touloub, was handed a 15-year sentence as an accomplice.
Four-year-old Inass Touloub was found along the A10 road in SuÃ¨vres in the Loir-et-Cher department on 11 August 1987. Her body bore multiple marks of abuse, including human bite marks, broken bones and burns with an iron.
She was buried in an unmarked grave near the location where her body was found. Unidentified for three decades, she was known only as the "Little Martyr of the A10".
Then, in 2018, she was identified after the DNA of her brother â tested in an unrelated case â matched with hers, leading to the arrest of their parents.
The trial took place in Loir-et-Cher Assize Court from 2 November, with the verdict delivered on Tuesday after several hours of deliberation.
During the trial, prosecutor AnaÃ¯s Allio emphasised that "not a single part of Inass's body was spared", and recalled the "sense of vertigo that overcame us all" upon viewing the "unbearable photographs" from the autopsy, France Info reports.
The jury concluded that the child's mother was suffering from impaired judgement at the time of the girl's death, which reduced the maximum potential sentence.
French media outlet France Info described the two defendants as sitting stoically in chairs before the court with their heads bowed as the reasoning behind the verdict was read out.
El Bakhti and Touloub have 10 days to appeal the verdict.
Inass's death sparked one of France's biggest ever investigations, with the girl's photograph posted in public places and an alert sent to more than 30 countries.

noticias.titulo: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be US Speaker of the House
noticias.resumen: The nomination sets him on the path to become the first black lawmaker to lead the chamber when Democrats take control of the House in January.
noticias.texto:
Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be US Speaker of the House
- Published
Democrats in the US House of Representatives officially nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be Speaker, setting him on the path to become the first black lawmaker to lead the chamber.
The House will elect its new Speaker on 3 January, when the next term begins and Democrats will be in the majority.
His election to the powerful position - the Speaker is in line to succeed the president after the vice-president - is widely expected. Should he win, Jeffries will preside over his party's largest House majority in years and benefit from the Senate also being under Democrats' control.
Jeffries told reporters after the vote that the nomination was "a high honour and a distinct privilege".
As of Wednesday, Democrats will hold at least 257 seats in the House next year, which is well beyond the 218 needed for a majority. Seven races from the recent midterm elections are still uncalled.
Jeffries, who represents a district in New York, was re-elected as the party leader in a 251-11 closed-door vote on Wednesday. He has served as minority leader since 2023.
Despite overwhelming support in Wednesday's vote, Jeffries faced a handful of holdouts from new members in the party's left wing, who have said the party's sweeping victory in the midterm elections is a sign voters want change.
"While we have seen meaningful progress, there is still work to be done to ensure that the direction our party takes in this coming Congress reflects what our constituents are demanding of our leadership," seven incoming lawmakers, including fellow New Yorkers Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez, said in a statement.
All congressional Democrats are gearing up for clashes with the White House once they officially take control in January.
President Donald Trump, a Republican, has signalled a willingness to work with Democrats on some issues, but has also pledged to use his veto power to reject legislation he does not like.
That could make it hard for Democrats to deliver on their campaign promises to address affordability and pass other reforms.
At a news conference following the vote on Wednesday, Jeffries pledged that House Democrats would "fight to lower the high costs of groceries and gas and housing", and "make healthcare affordable for every single American".
Though the party will have a large enough majority to weather defections on must-pass legislation, Jeffries will still have to navigate internal ideological divisions that have grown particularly sharp over US support of Israel and Americans' rising healthcare costs.
Many incoming Democrats, including members of the Democratic Socialists of America, won their elections by challenging the party establishment.
The Congressional Progressive Caucus, from the party's left wing, congratulated Jeffries on the nomination, adding they would "continue conversations with Leader Jeffries to ensure Democrats deliver a bold agenda for working people".
Along with shepherding legislation, Jeffries as Speaker will also have to manage the complex array of investigations that Democrats plan to launch into Trump, his family, and cabinet members now that they have regained control of the chamber's oversight powers.
Rounding out their party leadership team, House Democrats also elected Katherine Clark of Massachusetts as majority leader, Pete Aguilar of California as majority whip, and Joe Neguse of Colorado as assistant speaker.

noticias.titulo: Julio Iglesias facing court investigation over alleged sexual offences
noticias.resumen: The 83-year-old singer is accused of abusing two former employees at Caribbean residences in 2021.
noticias.texto:
Julio Iglesias facing court investigation over alleged sexual offences
- Published
Singer Julio Iglesias is facing an investigation by Spain's national court over allegations he sexually abused and assaulted two female former staff members
Two women, who worked for the 83-year-old in the Caribbean, have accused him of abuse which they say took place in the Bahamas and the Dominican Republic in 2021.
The announcement comes after Spanish prosecutors dropped an inquiry into the claims earlier this year after concluding that they lacked jurisdiction because the alleged crimes took place abroad.
Iglesias, who has been a household name in Spain since the 1960s and has sold millions of records worldwide, has previously denied the allegations.
But in a statement published on Wednesday, external (in Spanish), national court Judge Antonio PiÃ±a said the account given in the complaint, alongside preliminary evidence provided, justified opening criminal proceedings.
He added that the investigation would cover parts of the complaint relating to potential crimes against sexual freedom, as well as assault and degrading treatment.
But the court will not investigate claims made in the lawsuit of human trafficking or crimes against workers' rights. PiÃ±a said these allegations were dismissed after he looked into the hiring of the women and found there was "no deception or artifice involved".
PiÃ±a said the former employees had been summoned to testify in person on 3 February.
The announcement comes after Spain's public prosecutor's office shifted its position last month, saying it now believed the court had jurisdiction to investigate the allegations.
In its statement, the national court said Spanish law sets out that courts can hear cases of crimes committed abroad by Spanish citizens provided certain conditions are met.
The allegations against Iglesias first emerged in a joint three-year investigation between Spanish newspaper El Diario, external and television network Univision news, published in January.
In that investigation, the two women were identified as a domestic worker and a physical therapist, who described alleged sexual abuse and degrading working conditions.
The domestic worker, whose name was changed to Rebeca in the reports, said Iglesias would regularly call her to his room at the end of the day and would touch her inappropriately without consent.
Rebeca, a Dominican who was 22 when the alleged events took place, also alleged that Iglesias had forced her to take part in threesomes with another female member of staff. She also described the singer slapping her in the face and grabbing her genitals.
The other woman, a Venezuelan physical therapist named as Laura in the article, said Iglesias had touched her breasts and kissed her on the mouth against her will. She added that he constantly threatened to fire her, controlled how much food she ate and asked her about when her period was due.
Rebeca and Laura filed an initial legal complaint in January against Iglesias for sexual assault and human trafficking.
In a response to the allegations in January, Iglesias said, external: "I deny having abused, coerced, or disrespected any woman. These accusations are absolutely false and deeply sadden me."
On Wednesday, the court said the lawsuit had been accepted based on evidence provided in the complaint. This included a photograph of one of the complainants, showing a bruise on her arm that was "consistent with the possibility of her being grabbed forcefully".
It added that the same photo showed "two marks on one of her thighs that could correspond to a human bite", which the complainant said were "a consequence of her forced participation in acts of a sexual nature".
WhatsApp message exchanges, including New Year's greetings, which suggest an "affectionate" relationship between the women and Iglesias, will also be considered, the court said.
But it added that the seemingly cordial tone, which presents "an apparent discrepancy with certain aspects of the narrative", would be clarified through a "complete and contextualised examination of the communications".
The claim over violations of workers' rights could not be investigated because there is no comparable criminal offence in the Bahamas and the Dominican Republic, where the alleged crimes took place, it said.
Iglesias is one of the most successful Latin artists of all time, having sold more than 300 million records in a career spanning decades.
He is also the father of fellow music superstar Enrique Iglesias.
